1	# Dungeon Builder: the in-game authoring loop
     2	
     3	**Status:** approved target; delivery tracked by rpg-project#175 and PR #181
     4	
     5	The canonical target is [Specimen Pack v0.2](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/175#issuecomment-5185751479), superseding v0.1 as grammar authority. v0.1 remains historical delivery evidence only. The dungeon document remains `version: 1`.
     6	
     7	## Authority and model
     8	
     9	The editor writes canonical YAML; the toolkit validates, compiles, and owns rules; the API projects and orchestrates; the web renders authorized server truth. Current prototype behavior is not a compatibility contract.
    10	
    11	Physical geometry is independent of semantic regions. The prerequisite canvas is `canvas: {width, height}`, origin `[0,0]`, columns `[0,width)`, rows `[0,height)`, with positive dimensions. Source YAML supplies dimensions; the toolkit derives every in-bounds odd-q cell as structural floor. Authoring projection exposes those explicit canonical cells and canonical physical edges. There are no holes, masks, levels, rooms, connectors, or procedural-compatibility requirements in this target. Runtime is fog-authorized: it must not leak hidden extents.
    12	
    13	Regions are a flat authored list of complete absolute extents. The parent is the smallest strict superset; the innermost region is the smallest containing region. Disjoint regions are siblings; equal or partial overlap is invalid; no parent is authored. The unpainted root area remains valid content space. `archetype` is optional and inherits when omitted; an explicit value is limited to `entrance | chamber | corridor | boss`. Zero, one, or multiple explicitly declared regions of each archetype are runnable. `archetype: boss` labels a boss semantic scope only: it identifies neither a boss entity/cell nor a placed-monster marker, and creates no spawn behavior. Top-level `place:` monsters remain ordinary explicit placements. A root may resolve without an archetype absent a consumer default. Source persistence retains only irreducible region facts (`id`, `name`, archetype presence/value, and canonical source cells); parent relationships and the innermost index are recomputed on compile/load.
    14	
    15	Painting, repainting, or deleting a region cannot alter structural floor, canonical edges, endpoint-derived door IDs, content, or content validity; removed semantics fall back to the enclosing scope/root. Existing room-based semantic lookups are not renamed: after an existing path has an absolute location, it deliberately resolves scope from that location.
    16	
    17	Physical door identity is normalized from its endpoints and is region-independent. A physical lock, when authored, uses `lock.options` with one or more alternatives, each with a valid ability and positive DC; alternatives are ORed. Omitted lock means initially unlocked. Empty options and locks on non-door edges reject. Authoring projects every option when it exposes lock configuration; runtime gameplay may remain interaction-opaque. Lock behavior is a separate #175 follow-up, not Wave 0 or #180 acceptance.
    18	
    19	## Delivery waves
    20	
    21	**Wave 0 — roomless canvas vertical (prerequisite).** Deliver canvas dimensions, toolkit-derived floor cells, and edges in authoring proto, toolkit validation/compile/persistence, API projection, and fog-safe runtime geometry. Use unlocked doors in executable fixtures. This wave has no semantic-region scope.
    22	
    23	**Wave 1 — semantic scopes (#180).** Deliver region extents, derived containment and index, innermost/scope-path resolution, optional/inheriting archetypes, source persistence, authoring projection, `Zone.parent_id`, and fog-safe runtime projection. Run every structurally usable scope graph; report missing semantic conventions only through an existing surface when one exists. Do not add a boss entity/cell, boss marker on a placed monster, boss spawning, a diagnostics proto/API, future properties, hidden extents, or web implementation scope.
    24	
    25	For each wave, proto contract merges/releases before API consumer development/evidence; API states the provider need; toolkit releases; API pins released providers and merges last. One issue/branch/PR per repo per wave. None are created by this dispatch. PR #181 is the approved exception: it may merge before implementation so canonical docs and the living handoff reach `main`; Kirk alone decides and merges.
    26	
    27	## Non-goals and validation
    28	
    29	No room-first compilation authority, room-derived placement/spawn/door identity, room chains, connectedness requirement, rectangle compatibility, procedural compatibility, lighting/audio/trigger capabilities, new boss/spawn rules, geometry/traversal changes, holes, levels, lock behavior, or web implementation in #180. Preserve only a generic future extension seam and current location-to-scope lookup. #176–#179 are delivered/open history, not reopened. Wave 1 hard validation is limited to safely/deterministically representable source: strict YAML/types/coordinates, duplicate IDs, cells outside structural floor, incompatible non-empty `rooms:` plus `regions:`, unsupported explicit archetypes, and equal/partial overlaps. Duplicate cells within one region are canonically deduplicated; disconnected cells and missing semantic roles are runnable.
    30	
    31	## Evidence and pointers
    32	
    33	Delivered backend history: [rpg-api-protos#206](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api-protos/pull/206), [rpg-toolkit#881](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/881) with tags `tools/spatial/v0.6.0`, `rulebooks/dnd5e/v0.71.0`, and `encounter/v0.48.0`, and [rpg-api#769](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/pull/769) are delivery evidence (comment [5183123668](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/179#issuecomment-5183123668)). #176–#179 remain OPEN on GitHub but are delivered history; web is independently owned. Wave 0 is LIVE VERIFIED. Wave 1 implementation has not started; its acceptance is schema/toolkit/API wire and persistence evidence. See #175 and #180 for the live gate.
    34	
    35	Use the active role signature for future edits; do not hard-code an asset-pipeline signature.

    23	2. `rpg-api` states the provider need and consumes the released contract without deriving geometry or hidden extents.

    38	### Rejection classes
    39	
    40	Every construct in §2 is rejected by exactly one of three mechanisms:
    41	
    42	| Class | Mechanism | Example |
    43	|---|---|---|
    44	| 1 | Decode-known; `Validate` rejects at a field path | `mount:` — `PlacedEntry.Mount` decodes (`dungeonspec/spec.go:86`); rejected by path (`validate.go:351-353`) |
    45	| 2 | Not in schema; whole-document decode failure | `height:` on a placement — not a `PlacedEntry` field |
    46	| 3 | Decode-known; `Validate` accepts | every construct in §4 |
    47	
    48	§4.9's requirement that `mount: wall` fail with a field-path error (not a
    49	whole-document decode failure) depends on `mount:` being class 1, not class 2.

    51	## 3. Ground rules
    52	
    53	1. Decode is strict and single-document: `KnownFields(true)`; an unrecognized
    54	   top-level field MUST fail the whole document; multi-document input MUST be
    55	   rejected.
    56	2. `version:` MUST equal `1`. Any other value MUST be rejected.
    57	3. Every cell coordinate (`walls:`, `start:`, `place[].at`, `regions[].cells`) is
    58	   absolute pointy-top odd-q offset `[column,row]` — the same space a compiled
    59	   `FloorPlan` uses.
    60	4. Physical geometry (space/canvas/floor, canonical wall/door edges) and semantic
    61	   scope (regions, §4.10) are independent axes. Neither derives the other.
    62	
    63	## 4. Per-construct specification
    64	
    65	### 4.1 Document metadata
    66	
    67	```yaml
    68	version: 1
    69	key: shrine-hall
    70	name: 'The Shrine Hall'
    71	theme: crypt
    72	height: 8
    73	```
    74	
    75	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
    76	|---|---|---|---|
    77	| `version` | int | yes | MUST equal `1` |
    78	| `key` | string | yes | `[a-z0-9-]+`; MUST match the request key |
    79	| `name` | string | yes | non-empty |
    80	| `theme` | string | no | — |
    81	| `height` | int | decode-optional (missing → `0`) | room-chain mode: `Validate` requires `>= 4`. canvas mode: unvalidated and unused — `canvas.height` (§4.5) is authoritative; a value below `4` MUST NOT be rejected and MUST NOT affect canvas geometry |
    82	
    83	### 4.2 Room chain — `rooms:`
    84	
    85	```yaml
    86	rooms:
    87	  - id: antechamber
    88	    archetype: entrance   # entrance | chamber | corridor | boss
    89	    width: 6
    90	```
    91	
    92	1. `rooms:` MUST contain at least 2 entries.
    93	2. `start_column[i] = start_column[i-1] + width[i-1] + 1` (server-computed; the `+1`
    94	   reserves a connector-gap column).
    95	3. Exactly one room MUST have `archetype: boss` and MUST declare `boss:`. No other
    96	   room MAY declare `boss:`.
    97	4. A document combining non-empty `rooms:` with `regions:` is rejected (§4.10.3.6).
    98	   Region archetypes add no boss-cardinality, entrance, or spawn-rule enforcement
    99	   to the room-chain mode.
   100	
   101	### 4.3 Connectors — `connectors:`
   102	
   103	```yaml
   104	connectors:
   105	  - { from: antechamber, to: shrine }
   106	  - { from: shrine, to: vault, locked: { dc: 12, ability: dex } }
   107	```
   108	
   109	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   110	|---|---|---|---|
   111	| `from` | room id | yes | MUST equal `rooms[i].id` for connector index `i` |
   112	| `to` | room id | yes | MUST equal `rooms[i+1].id` for connector index `i` |
   113	| `locked` | object | no | `{dc, ability}`; omitted = unlocked |
   114	
   115	1. `connectors:` MUST contain exactly `len(rooms) - 1` entries.
   116	2. `from`/`to` are not independently authorable — only `locked:` varies per entry.
   117	3. A region-attachment door (§4.10.2) MUST NOT satisfy, replace, or count toward
   118	   this requirement.
   119	
   120	### 4.4 Room-scoped placement — `place:` / `boss:` / `obstacles:`
   121	
   122	```yaml
   123	rooms:
   124	  - id: hall
   125	    obstacles:
   126	      - { ref: 'dnd5e:props:bone-pile', count: 3 }
   127	    place:
   128	      - { ref: 'dnd5e:props:brazier', at: [1, 1], blocks_movement: true, blocks_los: false }
   129	    boss:
   130	      ref: 'dnd5e:monsters:skeleton-captain'
   131	      at: [4, 3]
   132	```
   133	
   134	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   135	|---|---|---|---|
   136	| `place[].ref` / `boss.ref` | string | yes | `dnd5e:props:*` or `dnd5e:monsters:*` |
   137	| `place[].at` / `boss.at` | `[int,int]` | yes | room-local `[col,row]`; MUST NOT be the door row |
   138	| `place[].blocks_movement` | bool | no | props only; MUST be rejected on a monster ref |
   139	| `place[].blocks_los` | bool | no | props only; MUST be rejected on a monster ref |
   140	| `place[].facing` | enum | no | see §4.9 for acceptance scope |
   141	| `obstacles[].ref` | string | yes | — |
   142	| `obstacles[].count` | int | yes | `>= 1` |
   143	
   144	1. `at` resolves to an absolute cell by adding the room's `start_column` (§4.2.2).
   145	2. The door row (`row == height/2`) MUST be rejected for `place[].at` and `boss.at`.
   146	3. Exactly one room MUST declare `boss:` (§4.2.3); there is no top-level `boss:` in
   147	   v0.3 (§4.6.2).
   148	
   149	### 4.5 Canvas — `canvas:` (rpg-project#192, Wave 0)
   150	
   151	```yaml
   152	canvas:
   153	  width: 20   # positive integer; columns [0, width)
   154	  height: 30  # positive integer; rows [0, height)
   155	rooms: []
   156	```
   157	
   158	1. A document is in exactly one of two floor-source modes: **room-chain mode**
   159	   (`rooms:` non-empty) or **canvas mode** (`canvas:` present, `rooms: []`).
   160	2. A document combining non-empty `rooms:` with `canvas:` MUST be rejected — a
   161	   document declares exactly one floor-source mode, never both.
   162	3. In canvas mode, the following checks MUST be skipped entirely: the `height >= 4`
   163	   check; the `len(rooms) >= 2` check; `connectors:` count-equals-`len(rooms)-1`;
   164	   boss cardinality; boss-axis; the M1 monster/boss.at restriction; boss-ref
   165	   validation. These seven MUST be skipped together — skipping boss cardinality
   166	   without the remaining boss-cluster checks produces undefined behavior against a
   167	   nil room reference.
   168	4. In canvas mode, static validation of `walls:` (§4.7) and `start:` (§4.8) MUST use
   169	   the canvas-derived floor (`[0,width) × [0,height)`) as their floor source, not the
   170	   room-chain floor.
   171	5. Independently of rule 4: persisted authored-edge validation at `InitDungeon` time
   172	   (the runtime-side check behind §4.7's endpoint-floor-membership requirement) MUST
   173	   ALSO use a canvas-derived floor source in canvas mode. This is a second,
   174	   separately-implemented check — extending the static path (rule 4) does not
   175	   extend this one.
   176	6. In-bounds checks otherwise run against `canvas.width`/`canvas.height`.
   177	7. Top-level `place:` (§4.6) MUST be accepted in canvas mode and MUST remain
   178	   rejected in room-chain mode.
   179	8. `start:` (§4.8) resolves against the canvas floor in canvas mode.
   180	9. `FloorPlan` MUST echo `rooms: []` plus `canvas.width`/`canvas.height`, with
   181	   authored edges present as usual, and MUST also project the canonical
   182	   structural-floor cells derived from the canvas dimensions.
   183	10. Growing `width`/`height` MUST be accepted unconditionally. Shrinking below any
   184	    existing placement, wall endpoint, `start:`, or region cell MUST be rejected with
   185	    a named, specific error — never a silent drop.
   186	11. Non-goals: no semantic-region/zone requirement (a canvas document with no
   187	    `regions:` treats its whole floor as the implicit root scope, §4.10.2.1); no
   188	    boss/monster content requirement; no locked-door grammar/binding decision beyond
   189	    §4.7.6.
   190	
   191	**Acceptance criteria:**
   192	- `PutDungeon(validate_only)` against `canvas: {width,height}`, `rooms: []` decodes
   193	  successfully and returns a compiled `FloorPlan`.
   194	- An in-bounds canvas document validates successfully; every room-chain-only rule is
   195	  skipped; out-of-bounds content fails clearly against canvas dimensions.
   196	- `FloorPlan` for a canvas document carries the projected canonical structural-floor
   197	  cell set, not dimensions alone.
   198	- A canvas document with top-level `height: 1` validates successfully.
   199	- A document declaring both non-empty `rooms:` and `canvas:` is rejected.
   200	- Shrinking `width`/`height` below existing content produces a named, specific
   201	  validation error, never a silent drop.
   202	
   203	### 4.6 Top-level placement — `place:` (canvas mode)
   204	
   205	```yaml
   206	canvas: { width: 20, height: 30 }
   207	rooms: []
   208	place:
   209	  - { ref: 'dnd5e:props:pillar', at: [10, 15] }
   210	  - { ref: 'dnd5e:props:altar', at: [8, 8], facing: W }
   211	  - { ref: 'dnd5e:monsters:skeleton-captain', at: [5, 18] }
   212	```
   213	
   214	Same field table as §4.4's `place[]`, except `at` is unconditionally absolute
   215	(no room `start_column` offset) and there is no owning room.
   216	
   217	1. MUST be accepted in canvas mode; MUST remain rejected in room-chain mode.
   218	2. There is no top-level `boss:` in v0.3 — `boss:` remains room-scoped only (§4.4.3).
   219	3. `facing:` on a non-monster, `mount: floor` entry MUST be accepted (§4.9.2).
   220	
   221	### 4.7 Walls — `walls:` (edge-native; rpg-project#176/#179)
   222	
   223	```yaml
   224	walls:
   225	  - { from: [7, 0], to: [7, 1], kind: solid }
   226	  - { from: [7, 4], to: [7, 5], kind: door }
   227	```
   228	
   229	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   230	|---|---|---|---|
   231	| `from` | `[int,int]` | yes | absolute `[col,row]`; distinct from and hex-adjacent to `to`; MUST be a floor cell of the active mode (§4.5) |
   232	| `to` | `[int,int]` | yes | same constraints as `from` |
   233	| `kind` | enum | yes | `solid \| door` |
   234	| `lock.options[]` | array | no; if present, `>= 1` entry | see below |
   235	| `lock.options[].ability` | string | yes (if `lock` present) | valid ability identifier |
   236	| `lock.options[].dc` | int | yes (if `lock` present) | `1–30` |
   237	
   238	1. Edge identity is undirected (normalized endpoint pair). A duplicate — including
   239	   the reversed pair — MUST be rejected.
   240	2. Both endpoints MUST be compiled floor cells of the active mode (§4.5).
   241	3. An authored `kind` MUST replace a colliding *generated, non-connector* edge. A
   242	   collision with a *connector-generated* edge MUST be rejected.
   243	4. Door identity MUST derive from `(dungeon key, normalized endpoint pair)`. An
   244	   authored door MUST start closed and unlocked. Interaction MUST be legal from
   245	   either endpoint.
   246	5. Runtime wall geometry is carried on `HexRecord.edges`. The flat
   247	   `EncounterService.Space.walls` field MUST NOT exist or be reintroduced. Shared
   248	   edges MUST be deduplicated, not assigned independently per side.
   249	6. `lock.options` grammar (shown above) is accepted for decode/round-trip but is
   250	   **not part of v0.3's acceptance criteria** — executable v0.3 fixtures MUST use
   251	   unlocked doors only. Lock *behavior* is out of scope for v0.3.
   252	
   253	**Acceptance criteria:**
   254	- Duplicate (including reversed), non-adjacent, and out-of-footprint edges MUST fail
   255	  validation clearly.
   256	- An authored door edge MUST NOT satisfy, replace, or count toward a chain
   257	  `connectors:` requirement.
   258	- An inner authored edge changes movement/LoS on both sides while every affected
   259	  cell retains its existing region membership unchanged (§4.10.3.6).
   260	
   261	### 4.8 Start — `start:` (rpg-project#177)
   262	
   263	```yaml
   264	start: [1, 3]   # absolute [column, row]; optional/null
   265	```
   266	
   267	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   268	|---|---|---|---|
   269	| `start` | `[int,int]` or `null` | no | absolute `[col,row]`; member of exactly one room's/region's floor footprint |
   270	
   271	1. Omitted or `null` MUST preserve today's generator-selected entrance exactly.
   272	2. MAY be in any semantic room/region regardless of archetype.
   273	3. The door row is legal for `start:` only (contrast §4.4.2). Connector-gap cells,
   274	   including the connector door cell, MUST be rejected.
   275	4. Resolves against the active floor source (§4.5).
   276	5. The toolkit MUST reserve the resolved anchor plus an ordered party envelope
   277	   (4 seats, the normal default `PartyCap`) before generating any blockers, for
   278	   every seed. A request exceeding the reserved seat count MUST return an explicit
   279	   requested-vs-available error, not a fallback or partial seating.
   280	6. `FloorPlan.entrance`/`SpaceData.Entrance` remain the sole resolved-anchor wire
   281	   field; with an authored `start:`, they MUST report the authored anchor verbatim,
   282	   including outside an entrance-archetype room.
   283	
   284	**Acceptance criteria:**
   285	- Omitted/`null` fixtures retain today's entrance/spawn/generation behavior exactly.
   286	- A door-row start in any semantic room/region validates; malformed shapes,
   287	  out-of-footprint cells, connector gaps, and ambiguous/no-room membership are
   288	  rejected.
   289	- `PutDungeon(validate_only)` wire `FloorPlan.entrance`, persisted
   290	  `SpaceData.Entrance`, and the first real `StartEncounter` player position MUST
   291	  agree on the authored absolute cell.
   292	
   293	### 4.9 Facing — `place:`/`boss:` `facing:` (rpg-project#178)
   294	
   295	```yaml
   296	- { ref: 'dnd5e:props:statue-reaper', at: [4, 1], facing: SE }
   297	```
   298	
   299	| Value | `E` | `NE` | `NW` | `W` | `SW` | `SE` |
   300	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   301	| Index | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
   302	
   303	1. `facing:` is decode-known on every `place:`/`boss:` entry type.
   304	2. Acceptance is scoped to non-monster, `mount: floor` (default) placements — MAY be
   305	   room-scoped, or top-level in canvas mode (§4.6). The capability belongs to the
   306	   placement (a floor prop), not to which list it lives in.
   307	3. A monster `place:` entry, a `boss:` entry, or a `mount: wall` placement with
   308	   `facing:` set MUST be rejected with a field-path-specific error (e.g.
   309	   `"facing only supported on floor props"`), not a decode failure and not a silent
   310	   drop.
   311	4. Current validator error order (fact, not a v0.3 change): `facing` is checked
   312	   before `mount`; the top-level-unsupported error fires only once no entry sets
   313	   either.
   314	5. Omitted/`null` MUST preserve existing orientation exactly; presence MUST be
   315	   distinguished from absence through persistence.
   316	
   317	**Acceptance criteria:**
   318	- All six values compile and render at the expected 60° orientations on a
   319	  room-scoped, non-monster, floor-mounted placement.
   320	- All six values compile and render identically on a canvas-mode top-level,
   321	  non-monster, floor-mounted placement.
   322	- An unknown value fails validation with the accepted vocabulary named in the error.
   323	- A monster, boss, or `mount: wall` entry with `facing:` set fails with the
   324	  field-path-specific message above, in either mode.
   325	
   326	### 4.10 Regions — `regions:` (rpg-project#180, Wave 1)
   327	
   328	#### 4.10.1 Shape
   329	
   330	```yaml
   331	regions:
   332	  - id: shrine-inner
   333	    name: 'Shrine — Inner Sanctum'
   334	    archetype: chamber
   335	    cells: [[9, 2], [9, 3], [9, 4], [10, 2], [10, 3], [10, 4]]
   336	```
   337	
   338	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   339	|---|---|---|---|
   340	| `id` | string | yes | unique within document |
   341	| `name` | string | no | display label; `id` used if omitted |
   342	| `archetype` | string | no | `entrance \| chamber \| corridor \| boss`; explicit empty string MUST be rejected; omitted resolves per §4.10.2.5 |
   343	| `cells` | `[[int,int]]` | yes | absolute `[col,row]` pairs on structural floor; duplicate pairs are canonically deduplicated; disconnected and empty sets are legal |
   344	
   345	`cells:` is the required wire representation. `extent: {min,max}` rectangles MUST
   346	NOT be accepted as region shape.
   347	
   348	#### 4.10.2 Model rules
   349	
   350	1. Every cell belongs to exactly one innermost region scope. Unpainted cells belong
   351	   to the implicit root scope. Any walkable cell, including doorway/connector cells,
   352	   MAY be a region member.
   353	2. Hierarchy MUST be derived from cell-set containment only — no `parent:` field.
   354	   For any two declared regions: disjoint cell sets = siblings (valid); one a strict
   355	   subset of the other = child/parent (valid); any other overlap (equal or partial)
   356	   MUST be rejected. A region's parent = the smallest strict superset among declared
   357	   regions, or root if none. An empty region has root as its parent and owns no
   358	   cell. A cell's innermost region = the smallest declared region containing it.
   359	3. Regions MAY nest to arbitrary depth.
   360	4. A region boundary exists wherever region membership changes (including
   361	   transitions to/from root). This boundary is semantic only and MUST NOT be
   362	   compiled into a `FloorPlanEdge` record. Traversability at a boundary is governed
   363	   exclusively by any independently-authored `walls:` edge there (§4.7).
   364	5. Each region property (currently: `archetype`) resolves independently by walking
   365	   the containment chain innermost → outward; the first scope in the chain that
   366	   declares the property wins; if none declare it, the root default (if any)
   367	   applies.
   368	6. **Future extension seam (non-normative).** A future enter/exit capability may

   371	7. `archetype` is an optional, inheriting scope property. An explicit value MUST be
   372	   one of `entrance | chamber | corridor | boss`; zero, one, or multiple explicitly
   373	   declared regions of each value are runnable. `archetype: boss` labels a boss

   375	   monster as boss, or add spawn behavior. A top-level `place:` monster remains an
   376	   explicit ordinary placement. Missing semantic roles or conventions are non-blocking
   377	   follow-up findings where an existing surface can report them; this wave adds no
   378	   diagnostics proto/API and makes none an acceptance requirement.

     1	# Dungeon YAML Spec v0.3 — context and rationale
     2	
     3	`spec.md` in this directory is the normative contract, **RATIFIED 2026-08-05**. This
     4	file is everything that isn't: what the spec is for, why it says what it says, what
     5	disagreements it found between sources, the ratification record, and where the
     6	executable examples live. Read `spec.md` to implement against; read this file to
     7	understand why `spec.md` looks the way it does.
     8	
     9	## What this is
    10	
    11	This is the versioned contract between the builder side (which authors the dialect
    12	ahead of what the platform compiles — `rpg-dnd5e-web`'s `TARGET-YAML.md`/specimens)
    13	and the platform side (`rpg-toolkit`/`rpg-api-protos`/`rpg-api`, which implements
    14	against a ratified level). Kirk's ruling (verbatim, rpg-project session): "a
    15	sustainable way forward is for us to create the 0.2 spec and then they can build for
    16	that... let's get a solid 0.2 or 0.3 spec and start from there."
    17	
    18	`spec.md` is the **contract baseline**; it is not itself a request for platform
    19	implementation, and it does not claim any implementation, test, or merge evidence.
    20	
    21	## Cadence, and document version vs. spec level
    22	
    23	The builder authors spec v*N*+1 while the platform implements spec v*N*. Proposals for
    24	the next level amend into a `vNext` draft. Version skew between what the builder has
    25	authored and what the platform has shipped is the **designed steady state**, not a
    26	defect to close — see `TARGET-YAML.md`'s "this gap is permanent, not a phase."
    27	
    28	**Do not conflate the dungeon YAML document's `version:` field with the spec level.**
    29	The document's own `version:` stays `1` for every construct in this spec, including
    30	everything newly promoted in the v0.3 cut. Per Kirk's settled additive model
    31	(rpg-project#175), a new optional field does not bump the document version; only a
    32	real incompatible/breaking change would, and none is proposed here. Spec levels (v0.1,
    33	v0.2, v0.3, ...) are contract/pack versions — they track how much of the dialect a
    34	conforming implementation is expected to accept, entirely independent of the one YAML
    35	`version:` integer a document carries. `spec.md`'s Ground Rules state the actual
    36	document-level requirement (`version:` must be exactly `1`); this paragraph is only
    37	explaining why that requirement doesn't change as the spec itself moves from v0.2 to
    38	v0.3 to v0.4.
    39	
    40	Aligns with, and adopts the version number of, `rpg-dnd5e-web`'s specimen pack
    41	(`src/concepts/dungeon-builder/specimens/`, currently v0.3) — going forward, spec vN
    42	and web-pack vN name the same contract level.
    43	
    44	## How to read `spec.md`
    45	
    46	`spec.md` is table- and rule-first: YAML shape blocks, field tables, numbered MUST/MUST
    47	NOT requirements, and acceptance criteria per construct. It carries no narrative, no
    48	"why," and no history. Before ratification, six questions genuinely weren't settled,
    49	and `spec.md` marked each **OPEN — pending ratification** with a one-line pointer into
    50	this file's Reconciliation notes rather than picking an answer. Kirk ratified all six
    51	on 2026-08-05 (Ratification record, next section) — `spec.md` now states every one of
    52	them as a normative rule directly, with no OPEN markers remaining. Code citations
    53	(`file.go:line`, function names, literal error strings) live in `spec.md` because they
    54	pin exact required behavior; GitHub comment/issue provenance ("per the 19:27 comment,"
    55	"the checkpoint says") lives here instead, because it explains where a rule came from
    56	rather than stating the rule itself.

    73	   spec's own recommendation verbatim. `spec.md` §4.10.3 states it as a MUST-reject
    74	   rule. Kirk's rationale, verbatim: "this is what I originally had in my head when
    75	   we came up with regions — I saw them as rooms in toolkit... being able to relax it
    76	   and not create something new if it ever comes up makes this an easy call." A
    77	   **future-relaxation path is named, not ruled out**: authored regions layered over
    78	   generated/chain content is a legitimate vNext proposal if a real use case appears,
    79	   and a chain-to-canvas converter (letting an author "promote" a `rooms:` document
    80	   into `canvas:` + `regions:` losslessly) is the tool that would make that relaxation
    81	   cheap — not a chain/region cross-validator.

    83	   this spec's own recommendation verbatim. `spec.md` §4.5 now requires `FloorPlan` to
    84	   project canonical structural-floor cells for a canvas document; `spec.md` §4.10.4

    86	   parent id. The former "not required by this list" hedge is removed from both
    87	   sections' acceptance criteria.

    89	   conditions `spec.md` §4.9 already applies to a room-scoped entry (non-monster,
    90	   `mount: floor`). This spec gave no recommendation; the platform team's rationale:
    91	   the capability belongs to a floor prop, not to room ownership — a placement's
    92	   entitlement to `facing:` was never really about which list it lives in.
    93	   `specimens/canvas.yaml:14`'s top-level altar (`facing: W`) is now conforming.
    94	
    95	## Supersession: the #175 Specimen Pack v0.2 lineage
    96	
    97	This spec supersedes the [Specimen Pack v0.2 comment](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/175#issuecomment-5185751479)
    98	lineage on rpg-project#175 as grammar/acceptance authority for `regions:` — most
    99	concretely, its `extent: {min,max}` rectangle grammar, which Kirk has ruled out.
   100	`cells:` (painted cell lists) is the wire representation, matching `rpg-dnd5e-web`'s
   101	`TARGET-YAML.md` and its live specimen pack. Full discussion, including the
   102	`design.md`/`plan.md` follow-up-edit debt this supersession created, is Reconciliation
   103	notes item 1 below — that debt was paid separately, rpg-project#195 / PR #196.
   104	
   105	## The two-floor-source finding
   106	
   107	`spec.md` §4.5 states, as bare rules, which validators canvas mode must skip entirely
   108	and which must switch their floor source. The underlying discovery is worth recording
   109	here because it's counterintuitive and easy to re-break: `dungeonspec.Validate` (v1,
   110	room-chain path) contains **two independently-implemented, room-only floor-derivation
   111	functions**, not one — `semanticFloorCells` (`validate.go:546-568`, used by
   112	`validateWalls`/`validateWallEndpoint`) and, in a different package entirely,
   113	`semanticDungeonFloorHexes` (`authored_edges.go:118-138`, used by `InitDungeon`'s
   114	`validateAndNormalizeAuthoredEdges` at persist time). Both hardcode the same
   115	room-chain arithmetic (room widths, left-to-right, minus the connector-gap column),
   116	and both need their own canvas-mode branch — extending one without the other leaves a
   117	silent gap at whichever validation path wasn't touched.
   118	
   119	The concrete, verified consequence: with `rooms: []`, both functions compute
   120	`totalWidth = 0`, which collapses every in-bounds column check to `[0,0)`. A
   121	canvas document's `walls:`/`start:` are not merely *unsupported* today — they are
   122	*rejected as out-of-bounds for every possible coordinate*, because the room-only
   123	math has nothing to range over. This is why `spec.md` states the floor-source swap as
   124	a requirement rather than a "nice to have": without it, canvas mode's own
   125	acceptance criteria (an in-bounds canvas document validates) are unreachable.
   126	
   127	The boss-cluster skip list has a parallel discovery. `validateBossCardinality`

   134	obstacles loop in `Validate`'s call order, which is probably why it reads as
   135	separate from the boss cluster rather than a third instance of the same hazard.
   136	
   137	## Regions: the scopes model, explained
   138	
   139	`spec.md` §4.10.2 states eight numbered MUST rules with no rationale attached. The
   140	rationale, settled across five comments on rpg-project#180
   141	(2026-08-04, 19:27–21:50 UTC — consumer position, refinement, representation/
   142	resolution, runtime convergence, platform decision checkpoint), is recorded here.
   143	
   144	**Hierarchy is derived from cell-set containment, never authored, and never a
   145	`parent:` field.** Four reasons, from the 19:52 comment: no donut problem (a parent's
   146	cells are its true full extent; deleting a child leaves the parent whole; repainting a
   147	child edits one list); the contradiction class (a child spilling outside its parent)
   148	is unrepresentable, since geometry is the only authority; a `parent:` field would
   149	duplicate what the cell sets already say, and duplicated truth drifts; flat lists keep
   150	diffs small and comments attached to the right list. Because overlap is allowed only

   152	regions sharing a cell must be nested, hence comparable. This is what makes "the
   153	parent" and "the innermost region" well-defined, cheap lookups rather than an
   154	ambiguous multi-parent graph.

   156	**Per-property resolution, illustrated.** The vault (innermost) declares `audio:` —

    38	### Rejection classes

    42	| Class | Mechanism | Example |

    51	## 3. Ground rules
    52	
    53	1. Decode is strict and single-document: `KnownFields(true)`; an unrecognized
    54	   top-level field MUST fail the whole document; multi-document input MUST be
    55	   rejected.

    58	   absolute pointy-top odd-q offset `[column,row]` — the same space a compiled
    59	   `FloorPlan` uses.
    60	4. Physical geometry (space/canvas/floor, canonical wall/door edges) and semantic

    62	
    63	## 4. Per-construct specification
    64	
    65	### 4.1 Document metadata
    66	
    67	```yaml
    68	version: 1
    69	key: shrine-hall
    70	name: 'The Shrine Hall'
    71	theme: crypt
    72	height: 8
    73	```
    74	
    75	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
    76	|---|---|---|---|
    77	| `version` | int | yes | MUST equal `1` |
    78	| `key` | string | yes | `[a-z0-9-]+`; MUST match the request key |
    79	| `name` | string | yes | non-empty |
    80	| `theme` | string | no | — |
    81	| `height` | int | decode-optional (missing → `0`) | room-chain mode: `Validate` requires `>= 4`. canvas mode: unvalidated and unused — `canvas.height` (§4.5) is authoritative; a value below `4` MUST NOT be rejected and MUST NOT affect canvas geometry |
    82	
    83	### 4.2 Room chain — `rooms:`
    84	
    85	```yaml
    86	rooms:
    87	  - id: antechamber
    88	    archetype: entrance   # entrance | chamber | corridor | boss
    89	    width: 6
    90	```
    91	
    92	1. `rooms:` MUST contain at least 2 entries.
    93	2. `start_column[i] = start_column[i-1] + width[i-1] + 1` (server-computed; the `+1`
    94	   reserves a connector-gap column).
    95	3. Exactly one room MUST have `archetype: boss` and MUST declare `boss:`. No other
    96	   room MAY declare `boss:`.
    97	4. A document combining non-empty `rooms:` with `regions:` is rejected (§4.10.3.6).
    98	   Region archetypes add no boss-cardinality, entrance, or spawn-rule enforcement
    99	   to the room-chain mode.
   100	
   101	### 4.3 Connectors — `connectors:`
   102	
   103	```yaml
   104	connectors:
   105	  - { from: antechamber, to: shrine }
   106	  - { from: shrine, to: vault, locked: { dc: 12, ability: dex } }
   107	```

   109	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   110	|---|---|---|---|
   111	| `from` | room id | yes | MUST equal `rooms[i].id` for connector index `i` |
   112	| `to` | room id | yes | MUST equal `rooms[i+1].id` for connector index `i` |
   113	| `locked` | object | no | `{dc, ability}`; omitted = unlocked |
   114	
   115	1. `connectors:` MUST contain exactly `len(rooms) - 1` entries.
   116	2. `from`/`to` are not independently authorable — only `locked:` varies per entry.
   117	3. A region-attachment door (§4.10.2) MUST NOT satisfy, replace, or count toward
   118	   this requirement.
   119	
   120	### 4.4 Room-scoped placement — `place:` / `boss:` / `obstacles:`
   121	
   122	```yaml
   123	rooms:
   124	  - id: hall
   125	    obstacles:
   126	      - { ref: 'dnd5e:props:bone-pile', count: 3 }
   127	    place:
   128	      - { ref: 'dnd5e:props:brazier', at: [1, 1], blocks_movement: true, blocks_los: false }
   129	    boss:
   130	      ref: 'dnd5e:monsters:skeleton-captain'

   134	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   135	|---|---|---|---|
   136	| `place[].ref` / `boss.ref` | string | yes | `dnd5e:props:*` or `dnd5e:monsters:*` |
   137	| `place[].at` / `boss.at` | `[int,int]` | yes | room-local `[col,row]`; MUST NOT be the door row |

   139	| `place[].blocks_los` | bool | no | props only; MUST be rejected on a monster ref |

   141	| `obstacles[].ref` | string | yes | — |
   142	| `obstacles[].count` | int | yes | `>= 1` |

   144	1. `at` resolves to an absolute cell by adding the room's `start_column` (§4.2.2).

   148	
   149	### 4.5 Canvas — `canvas:` (rpg-project#192, Wave 0)
   150	
   151	```yaml
   152	canvas:
   153	  width: 20   # positive integer; columns [0, width)
   154	  height: 30  # positive integer; rows [0, height)
   155	rooms: []
   156	```

   158	1. A document is in exactly one of two floor-source modes: **room-chain mode**
   159	   (`rooms:` non-empty) or **canvas mode** (`canvas:` present, `rooms: []`).
   160	2. A document combining non-empty `rooms:` with `canvas:` MUST be rejected — a
   161	   document declares exactly one floor-source mode, never both.

   221	### 4.7 Walls — `walls:` (edge-native; rpg-project#176/#179)
   222	
   223	```yaml
   224	walls:

   230	|---|---|---|---|
   231	| `from` | `[int,int]` | yes | absolute `[col,row]`; distinct from and hex-adjacent to `to`; MUST be a floor cell of the active mode (§4.5) |

   234	| `lock.options[]` | array | no; if present, `>= 1` entry | see below |
   235	| `lock.options[].ability` | string | yes (if `lock` present) | valid ability identifier |

   237	
   238	1. Edge identity is undirected (normalized endpoint pair). A duplicate — including
   239	   the reversed pair — MUST be rejected.
   240	2. Both endpoints MUST be compiled floor cells of the active mode (§4.5).
   241	3. An authored `kind` MUST replace a colliding *generated, non-connector* edge. A
   242	   collision with a *connector-generated* edge MUST be rejected.
   243	4. Door identity MUST derive from `(dungeon key, normalized endpoint pair)`. An
   244	   authored door MUST start closed and unlocked. Interaction MUST be legal from

   254	- Duplicate (including reversed), non-adjacent, and out-of-footprint edges MUST fail
   255	  validation clearly.
   256	- An authored door edge MUST NOT satisfy, replace, or count toward a chain
   257	  `connectors:` requirement.
   258	- An inner authored edge changes movement/LoS on both sides while every affected

   261	### 4.8 Start — `start:` (rpg-project#177)
   262	
   263	```yaml
   264	start: [1, 3]   # absolute [column, row]; optional/null
   265	```

   267	| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
   268	|---|---|---|---|
   269	| `start` | `[int,int]` or `null` | no | absolute `[col,row]`; member of exactly one room's/region's floor footprint |
   270

   272	2. MAY be in any semantic room/region regardless of archetype.
   273	3. The door row is legal for `start:` only (contrast §4.4.2). Connector-gap cells,
   274	   including the connector door cell, MUST be rejected.
   275	4. Resolves against the active floor source (§4.5).
   276	5. The toolkit MUST reserve the resolved anchor plus an ordered party envelope
   277	   (4 seats, the normal default `PartyCap`) before generating any blockers, for
   278	   every seed. A request exceeding the reserved seat count MUST return an explicit
   279	   requested-vs-available error, not a fallback or partial seating.
   280	6. `FloorPlan.entrance`/`SpaceData.Entrance` remain the sole resolved-anchor wire
   281	   field; with an authored `start:`, they MUST report the authored anchor verbatim,
   282	   including outside an entrance-archetype room.
   283	
   284	**Acceptance criteria:**
   285	- Omitted/`null` fixtures retain today's entrance/spawn/generation behavior exactly.
   286	- A door-row start in any semantic room/region validates; malformed shapes,
   287	  out-of-footprint cells, connector gaps, and ambiguous/no-room membership are
   288	  rejected.
   289	- `PutDungeon(validate_only)` wire `FloorPlan.entrance`, persisted
   290	  `SpaceData.Entrance`, and the first real `StartEncounter` player position MUST
   291	  agree on the authored absolute cell.
   292	
   293	### 4.9 Facing — `place:`/`boss:` `facing:` (rpg-project#178)
   294	
   295	```yaml
   296	- { ref: 'dnd5e:props:statue-reaper', at: [4, 1], facing: SE }
   297	```
   298	
   299	| Value | `E` | `NE` | `NW` | `W` | `SW` | `SE` |
   300	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   301	| Index | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
   302	
   303	1. `facing:` is decode-known on every `place:`/`boss:` entry type.
   304	2. Acceptance is scoped to non-monster, `mount: floor` (default) placements — MAY be
   305	   room-scoped, or top-level in canvas mode (§4.6). The capability belongs to the
   306	   placement (a floor prop), not to which list it lives in.
   307	3. A monster `place:` entry, a `boss:` entry, or a `mount: wall` placement with
   308	   `facing:` set MUST be rejected with a field-path-specific error (e.g.
   309	   `"facing only supported on floor props"`), not a decode failure and not a silent
   310	   drop.
   311	4. Current validator error order (fact, not a v0.3 change): `facing` is checked
   312	   before `mount`; the top-level-unsupported error fires only once no entry sets
   313	   either.
   314	5. Omitted/`null` MUST preserve existing orientation exactly; presence MUST be
   315	   distinguished from absence through persistence.
   316	
   317	**Acceptance criteria:**
   318	- All six values compile and render at the expected 60° orientations on a
   319	  room-scoped, non-monster, floor-mounted placement.
   320	- All six values compile and render identically on a canvas-mode top-level,
   321	  non-monster, floor-mounted placement.
   322	- An unknown value fails validation with the accepted vocabulary named in the error.
   323	- A monster, boss, or `mount: wall` entry with `facing:` set fails with the
   324	  field-path-specific message above, in either mode.
   325	
   326	### 4.10 Regions — `regions:` (rpg-project#180, Wave 1)
   327	
   328	#### 4.10.1 Shape
   329	
   330	```yaml
   331	regions:
   332	  - id: shrine-inner
   333	    name: 'Shrine — Inner Sanctum'

1	# Dungeon YAML Spec v0.4
     2	
     3	**Status:** RATIFIED v0.4, 2026-08-08.
     4	**Normative delta.** RATIFIED v0.3
     5	([`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md)) remains the complete baseline. This file
     6	changes only the constructs and rules it names. Unmentioned v0.3 grammar and behavior
     7	remain normative. Context copied here is for reading continuity, not a claim that this
     8	file restates every v0.3 field.
     9	
    10	See [`README.md`](README.md) for evidence, reconciliation, and ratification history.
    11	
    12	## 1. Three distinct axes
    13	
    14	| Axis | Value | Meaning |
    15	|---|---|---|
    16	| Documentation cut | v0.4 | This proposal/review surface; never a YAML field. |
    17	| Dungeon document version | `version: 1` | Unchanged persisted YAML decode version. |
    18	| Canvas floor source | `canvas.floor_source: bounds \| regions` | Canvas topology only; omission resolves to `bounds`. |
    19	
    20	There is no `spec:` field. `spec: "0.4"`, `spec: draft`, and other documentation or
    21	workflow markers MUST fail strict decode. Behavior and environment fields are
    22	additive and independent of canvas floor-source choice.
    23	
    24	## 2. Additive transport shapes and capability behavior
    25	
    26	v0.4 adds four separable shapes. Each section defines decode/validation,
    27	preservation, authoring projection, runtime transport, and mechanical boundary.
    28	
    29	| Tranche | Authored shape | Authoring/runtime transport |
    30	|---|---|---|
    31	| A — region floor | `canvas.floor_source: regions` + `regions[].cells` | resolved source, full `FloorPlan.floor_cells`/pair `edges`/optional entrance; encounter snapshot uses the same mask/edges |
    32	| B — placement offset | optional `offset: [x,y,z]` | preserved on `FloorPlan.placements[]` and authorized runtime placement |
    33	| C — monster config | optional `target`, `profile`, `params` + exact-ref defaults | authored values compile into provider/spawn config; props reject |
    34	| D — lighting | optional root/region `lighting.ambient` | raw declarations plus optional inherited override; authorized runtime hex override |
    35	
    36	Capability detection uses the normal authoring path, not a new capability system. The
    37	builder sends the **exact candidate document** with
    38	`AuthoringService.PutDungeon(validate_only=true)`. Unsupported fields or values fail
    39	loudly through the ordinary response and source-path errors. A successful response
    40	returns the projection defined by the relevant section.
    41	
    42	Unsupported or not-yet-accepted semantics hard-stop preview/save/run. No layer may
    43	strip fields, substitute bounds floor, resolve opaque behavior in the client, or erase
    44	an offset/lighting override to make a request pass. Client-local conveniences may
    45	compile losslessly to canonical fields only as §8 permits.
    46	
    47	## 3. Shared delta rules
    48	
    49	1. Decode remains strict, known-field, and single-document. `version:` remains exactly
    50	   `1`.
    51	2. Coordinates remain pointy-top odd-q offset `[column,row]`. Room `place[].at` and
    52	   `boss.at` remain room-local source coordinates; their projection is absolute.
    53	3. The compiler validates and derives the canonical result. The API carries request
    54	   and result fields without reinterpreting them. The web authors values and renders
    55	   authorized projection.
    56	4. Field errors introduced by v0.4 MUST populate existing
    57	   `ValidationError.field` with the canonical source path. Authoring-derived records
    58	   call the same value `source_path`. Placement roots are `place[i]`,
    59	   `rooms[r].place[i]`, or `rooms[r].boss`; errors append the full nested suffix
    60	   (for example `rooms[1].place[0].params.example_key`).
    61	5. All writes are atomic. Failure leaves authored content and registry state
    62	   unchanged.
    63	
    64	## 4. Tranche A — region-union structural floor
    65	
    66	### 4.1 Canvas discriminator and floor modes
    67	
    68	```yaml
    69	canvas:
    70	  width: 12
    71	  height: 8
    72	  floor_source: regions
    73	rooms: []
    74	```
    75	
    76	`canvas.floor_source` is optional enum `bounds | regions`:
    77	
    78	- omitted or `bounds`: the v0.3 full `[0,width) × [0,height)` rectangle;
    79	- `regions`: the canonical deduplicated union of all `regions[].cells`.
    80	
    81	Canvas dimensions remain positive workspace/coordinate-legality bounds in either
    82	case. Under `regions`, an in-bounds cell outside the union is void, not root floor.
    83	The v0.3 topology matrix is unchanged: canvas requires explicit `rooms: []`; non-empty
    84	rooms forbid canvas and regions; regions without canvas reject. Room-chain generated
    85	floor is not affected.
    86	
    87	### 4.2 Regions and containment
    88	
    89	The v0.3 region source shape remains `id`, optional `name`, optional/inheriting
    90	`archetype`, and required absolute `cells`. Tranche D adds optional `lighting`.
    91	`extent`, polygons, authored parent, and authored derived indices remain invalid.
    92	
    93	1. Same-region duplicate cells canonicalize. A single empty region is legal and has
    94	   root parent.
    95	2. Between distinct regions, disjoint or strict containment is legal. Equal cell sets
    96	   and partial overlap reject. **Two empty regions are equal sets and therefore
    97	   reject**; the single-empty exception does not make multiple empty regions valid.
    98	3. Parent is the smallest strict non-empty superset, or root. Empty's parent is root.
    99	   Innermost ownership and parent/index are deterministic derived state.
   100	4. Region boundaries remain semantic and never create interior walls. Archetype
   101	   remains an inheriting label and creates no boss/spawn/content rule.
   102	5. Under `bounds`, unpainted floor is root. Under `regions`, unpainted cells are void;
   103	   root is hierarchy-only.
   104	
   105	### 4.3 Canonical mask and mechanics
   106	
   107	A canvas compile creates one canonical sorted floor mask from bounds or region union.
   108	All mechanical consumers use that compiled mask: validation, pathing, movement,
   109	placement, target reachability, start/party seating, LoS, reveal,
   110	fog, encounter initialization, and projection. No subsystem re-derives a rectangle
   111	or union for itself.
   112	
   113	`FloorPlan.floor_cells` is the complete authoring mask, sorted ascending
   114	`(column,row)`. Runtime exposes only authorized hexes, but every runtime floor hex
   115	comes from the encounter snapshot's same mask.
   116	
   117	### 4.4 Envelope edges reuse the existing pair projection
   118	
   119	Every hex side with exactly one floor endpoint and one void/off-canvas endpoint is an
   120	implicit generated solid envelope. This includes the outer boundary and an interior
   121	void boundary. It blocks movement and LoS exactly like other canonical solid edges.
   122	
   123	`FloorPlan.edges` reuses the existing flat `{from,to,kind}` pair representation:
   124	
   125	1. an envelope pair has exactly one endpoint in `FloorPlan.floor_cells`; that endpoint
   126	   owns the envelope edge;
   127	2. the other endpoint is the adjacent odd-q coordinate, whether an in-canvas void or
   128	   an off-canvas coordinate (negative or at/exceeding a bound);
   129	3. endpoint order is nonsemantic; consumers MUST determine ownership by membership in
   130	   `floor_cells`;
   131	4. `kind` is `solid`; the pair is normalized/deduplicated under the existing
   132	   undirected identity rule;
   133	5. runtime attaches the edge only to the owning floor `HexRecord`. There is no void
   134	   `HexRecord` and no duplicate attachment on another hex.
   135	
   136	Interior authored `walls:` retains v0.3 source validation: both endpoints are
   137	adjacent floor cells, duplicates reject, door identity is normalized endpoint-based,
   138	and runtime uses `HexRecord.edges`. No authored envelope door exists because a door
   139	requires floor on both sides.
   140	
   141	The existing authoring pair projection therefore needs no open wire decision. A
   142	one-cell region floor has six projected pairs; an interior one-cell void has six
   143	owning-floor pairs around it; an off-canvas side uses its actual adjacent coordinate.
   144	
   145	### 4.5 Draft validation, entrance presence, and runnable strictness
   146	
   147	`PutDungeon(validate_only=true)` accepts every structurally valid mask, including:
   148	
   149	- empty floor;
   150	- non-empty floor too small for `PartyCap`;
   151	- disconnected floor components.
   152	
   153	It always returns the canonical floor and envelope. `FloorPlan.entrance` has normative
   154	presence:
   155	
   156	- with authored `start`, **present** at that cell only when its ordered PartyCap
   157	  seating envelope lies wholly inside the same floor-cell connected component;
   158	  otherwise absent during validate-only;
   159	- with omitted/null `start`, **present** at the first qualifying anchor in ascending
   160	  `(column,row)` order;
   161	- **absent** when no qualifying anchor exists.
   162	
   163	A floor component is defined by hex-cell adjacency in the mask, independent of wall
   164	or door state. Every reserved seat MUST be a member of the anchor component. The
   165	existing deterministic PartyCap seat-order rule is reused; no seed or random fallback
   166	may choose another entrance.
   167	
   168	A non-validate write/registration and encounter start are strict. They require:
   169	
   170	1. non-empty floor;
   171	2. present resolved entrance and complete PartyCap envelope;
   172	3. every floor cell belongs to the entrance component (connected floor for this cut);
   173	4. every placement, authored edge endpoint, and start is valid against the compiled
   174	   mask/edges.
   175	
   176	Thus disconnected drafts preview but do not run. An entrance present on one island
   177	does not make a second island runnable. Non-validate failure is specific and atomic.
   178	Legacy bounds/room omitted-start behavior remains v0.3-compatible; these lifecycle
   179	rules apply to `floor_source: regions`.
   180	
   181	### 4.6 Candidate edits
   182	
   183	A region-cell or canvas-bound edit compiles the complete candidate before mutation.
   184	It recomputes mask, envelope, containment, entrance, PartyCap seating, lighting, and
   185	dependent content. A prior derived entrance/seat envelope is not authored content and
   186	is never an edit dependency: discard it, recompute from the candidate, and permit it
   187	to change. Only the freshly resolved candidate entrance/seats are authoritative for
   188	future authored registrations.
   189	
   190	A strict write rejects when the candidate fails §4.5 runnable conditions or removed
   191	floor invalidates an explicitly authored `start`, placement/monster/boss, or authored
   192	edge. No authored content moves, disappears, becomes root content,
   193	or falls back to bounds. If a region edit leaves the union unchanged (for example,
   194	deleting a nested scope whose cells remain in its parent), semantic properties may
   195	inherit outward. If the union changes and all strict candidate conditions pass,
   196	write/registration replaces atomically. Validate-only may return a structurally valid
   197	but non-runnable candidate as §4.5 defines.
   198	
   199	### 4.7 Authored content versus encounter persistence
   200	
   201	There are two lifecycles, not two competing floor authorities:
   202	
   203	- **Authored content load/write:** YAML is the source. `PutDungeon` non-validate and
   204	  startup/content discovery decode and compile the YAML, then atomically replace the
   205	  authored-dungeon registry state only after the full candidate succeeds. No prior
   206	  compiled floor cache is treated as authoring authority.
   207	- **Running encounter snapshot:** encounter creation copies the exact resolved mask,
   208	  canonical edges, entrance, placements, behavior config, and lighting it started
   209	  with into encounter persistence. Encounter reload uses that snapshot and validates
   210	  its internal consistency (edge ownership/deduplication, entrance/seats/entities on
   211	  snapshot floor, authorized records). It MUST NOT compare against or recompile the
   212	  current authored YAML. Later authored edits do not reshape an in-progress
   213	  encounter.
   214	
   215	This gives authored reload current source truth and encounter reload stable started
   216	truth without a source-versus-snapshot disagreement policy.
   217	
   218	### 4.8 Tranche A projection
   219	
   220	Authoring `FloorPlan` MUST carry:
   221	
   222	- resolved `floor_source` (`bounds` or `regions`, including resolved omission);
   223	- full canonical `floor_cells`;
   224	- full canonical flat pair `edges`, including envelope pairs;
   225	- optional-presence `entrance` per §4.5;
   226	- v0.3 region source plus derived parent/innermost projection.
   227	
   228	Runtime continues fog-authorized `HexRecord`/zone projection. An envelope is attached
   229	only to its authorized owning floor record. Hidden floor cells, edges, and zones are
   230	not globally exposed.
   231	
   232	## 5. Tranche B — placement `offset`
   233	
   234	### 5.1 Shape and applicability
   235	
   236	Any room-scoped or canvas top-level `place:` entry, and room `boss:`, may carry:
   237	
   238	```yaml
   239	offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.2]
   240	```
   241	
   242	`offset` is exactly three finite numbers `[x,y,z]`. Components are game-world units on
   243	the game's existing world axes and are relative to the placement's canonical compiled
   244	origin. The triple is world-axis-aligned; facing does not rotate or reinterpret it.
   245	Omission means `[0,0,0]` without creating an authored value.
   246	
   247	Existing `ref`, `at`, `facing`, `mount`, blocker, placement-location, and boss rules
   248	remain unchanged and apply independently. `offset` does not make an otherwise invalid
   249	`facing` or `mount` combination valid.
   250	
   251	### 5.2 Preservation, projection, and mechanics
   252	
   253	The compiler/server MUST preserve an authored triple verbatim through source
   254	persistence, authored-content reload, and encounter creation. It performs no pivot,
   255	attachment, snapping, bounding, or asset-specific correction.
   256	
   257	Authoring `FloorPlan.placements[]` returns `source_path`, `ref`, compiled absolute
   258	`at`, applicable existing facing/mount fields, and optional authored `offset`.
   259	Runtime returns the same optional triple on the authorized placement in
   260	`HexRecord.contents[]`. Builder and game apply that identical triple to the canonical
   261	placement origin.
   262	
   263	`offset` is cosmetic. It MUST NOT change the owning cell, structural floor, collision,
   264	`blocks_movement`, `blocks_los`, pathing, range, targetability, LoS, visibility, fog,
   265	or interaction identity. Authored blocker fields remain the sole prop mechanics.
   266	
   267	A client changing `ref` submits a complete edited document. It may retain, change, or
   268	remove `offset` explicitly. There is no server replacement command or stable placement ID. Asset-specific render
   269	behavior, raw matrices/quaternions, and uncommitted nudge state remain client-local.
   270	
   271	## 6. Tranche C — provider-defined monster config transport
   272	
   273	### 6.1 Source and applicability
   274	
   275	Every monster room `place`, canvas `place`, and room `boss` accepts flat optional:
   276	
   277	```yaml
   278	target: wounded
   279	profile: cautious
   280	params:

   139	requires floor on both sides.
   140	
   141	The existing authoring pair projection therefore needs no open wire decision. A
   142	one-cell region floor has six projected pairs; an interior one-cell void has six
   143	owning-floor pairs around it; an off-canvas side uses its actual adjacent coordinate.
   144	
   145	### 4.5 Draft validation, entrance presence, and runnable strictness
   146	
   147	`PutDungeon(validate_only=true)` accepts every structurally valid mask, including:
   148	
   149	- empty floor;
   150	- non-empty floor too small for `PartyCap`;
   151	- disconnected floor components.
   152	
   153	It always returns the canonical floor and envelope. `FloorPlan.entrance` has normative
   154	presence:
   155	
   156	- with authored `start`, **present** at that cell only when its ordered PartyCap
   157	  seating envelope lies wholly inside the same floor-cell connected component;
   158	  otherwise absent during validate-only;
   159	- with omitted/null `start`, **present** at the first qualifying anchor in ascending
   160	  `(column,row)` order;
   161	- **absent** when no qualifying anchor exists.
   162	
   163	A floor component is defined by hex-cell adjacency in the mask, independent of wall
   164	or door state. Every reserved seat MUST be a member of the anchor component. The
   165	existing deterministic PartyCap seat-order rule is reused; no seed or random fallback
   166	may choose another entrance.
   167	
   168	A non-validate write/registration and encounter start are strict. They require:
   169	
   170	1. non-empty floor;
   171	2. present resolved entrance and complete PartyCap envelope;
   172	3. every floor cell belongs to the entrance component (connected floor for this cut);
   173	4. every placement, authored edge endpoint, and start is valid against the compiled
   174	   mask/edges.
   175	
   176	Thus disconnected drafts preview but do not run. An entrance present on one island
   177	does not make a second island runnable. Non-validate failure is specific and atomic.
   178	Legacy bounds/room omitted-start behavior remains v0.3-compatible; these lifecycle
   179	rules apply to `floor_source: regions`.
   180	
   181	### 4.6 Candidate edits
   182	
   183	A region-cell or canvas-bound edit compiles the complete candidate before mutation.
   184	It recomputes mask, envelope, containment, entrance, PartyCap seating, lighting, and
   185	dependent content. A prior derived entrance/seat envelope is not authored content and
   186	is never an edit dependency: discard it, recompute from the candidate, and permit it
   187	to change. Only the freshly resolved candidate entrance/seats are authoritative for
   188	future authored registrations.
   189	
   190	A strict write rejects when the candidate fails §4.5 runnable conditions or removed
   191	floor invalidates an explicitly authored `start`, placement/monster/boss, or authored
   192	edge. No authored content moves, disappears, becomes root content,
   193	or falls back to bounds. If a region edit leaves the union unchanged (for example,
   194	deleting a nested scope whose cells remain in its parent), semantic properties may
   195	inherit outward. If the union changes and all strict candidate conditions pass,
   196	write/registration replaces atomically. Validate-only may return a structurally valid
   197	but non-runnable candidate as §4.5 defines.
   198	
   199	### 4.7 Authored content versus encounter persistence
   200	
   201	There are two lifecycles, not two competing floor authorities:
   202	
   203	- **Authored content load/write:** YAML is the source. `PutDungeon` non-validate and
   204	  startup/content discovery decode and compile the YAML, then atomically replace the
   205	  authored-dungeon registry state only after the full candidate succeeds. No prior
   206	  compiled floor cache is treated as authoring authority.
   207	- **Running encounter snapshot:** encounter creation copies the exact resolved mask,
   208	  canonical edges, entrance, placements, behavior config, and lighting it started
   209	  with into encounter persistence. Encounter reload uses that snapshot and validates
   210	  its internal consistency (edge ownership/deduplication, entrance/seats/entities on
   211	  snapshot floor, authorized records). It MUST NOT compare against or recompile the
   212	  current authored YAML. Later authored edits do not reshape an in-progress
   213	  encounter.
   214	
   215	This gives authored reload current source truth and encounter reload stable started
   216	truth without a source-versus-snapshot disagreement policy.
   217	
   218	### 4.8 Tranche A projection
   219	
   220	Authoring `FloorPlan` MUST carry:
   221	
   222	- resolved `floor_source` (`bounds` or `regions`, including resolved omission);
   223	- full canonical `floor_cells`;
   224	- full canonical flat pair `edges`, including envelope pairs;
   225	- optional-presence `entrance` per §4.5;
   226	- v0.3 region source plus derived parent/innermost projection.
   227	
   228	Runtime continues fog-authorized `HexRecord`/zone projection. An envelope is attached
   229	only to its authorized owning floor record. Hidden floor cells, edges, and zones are
   230	not globally exposed.
   231	
   232	## 5. Tranche B — placement `offset`
   233	
   234	### 5.1 Shape and applicability
   235	
   236	Any room-scoped or canvas top-level `place:` entry, and room `boss:`, may carry:
   237	
   238	```yaml
   239	offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.2]
   240	```
   241	
   242	`offset` is exactly three finite numbers `[x,y,z]`. Components are game-world units on
   243	the game's existing world axes and are relative to the placement's canonical compiled
   244	origin. The triple is world-axis-aligned; facing does not rotate or reinterpret it.
   245	Omission means `[0,0,0]` without creating an authored value.
   246	
   247	Existing `ref`, `at`, `facing`, `mount`, blocker, placement-location, and boss rules
   248	remain unchanged and apply independently. `offset` does not make an otherwise invalid
   249	`facing` or `mount` combination valid.
   250	
   251	### 5.2 Preservation, projection, and mechanics
   252	
   253	The compiler/server MUST preserve an authored triple verbatim through source
   254	persistence, authored-content reload, and encounter creation. It performs no pivot,
   255	attachment, snapping, bounding, or asset-specific correction.
   256	
   257	Authoring `FloorPlan.placements[]` returns `source_path`, `ref`, compiled absolute
   258	`at`, applicable existing facing/mount fields, and optional authored `offset`.
   259	Runtime returns the same optional triple on the authorized placement in
   260	`HexRecord.contents[]`. Builder and game apply that identical triple to the canonical
   261	placement origin.
   262	
   263	`offset` is cosmetic. It MUST NOT change the owning cell, structural floor, collision,
   264	`blocks_movement`, `blocks_los`, pathing, range, targetability, LoS, visibility, fog,
   265	or interaction identity. Authored blocker fields remain the sole prop mechanics.
   266	
   267	A client changing `ref` submits a complete edited document. It may retain, change, or
   268	remove `offset` explicitly. There is no server replacement command or stable placement ID. Asset-specific render
   269	behavior, raw matrices/quaternions, and uncommitted nudge state remain client-local.
   270	
   271	## 6. Tranche C — provider-defined monster config transport
   272	
   273	### 6.1 Source and applicability
   274	
   275	Every monster room `place`, canvas `place`, and room `boss` accepts flat optional:
   276	
   277	```yaml
   278	target: wounded
   279	profile: cautious
   280	params:

text:
281	  retreat_threshold: 0
   282	  announce: false
   283	```
   284	
   285	| Field | Shape |
   286	|---|---|
   287	| `target` | non-empty string |
   288	| `profile` | non-empty string |
   289	| `params` | map of non-empty string key to JSON scalar bool, string, or finite number |
   290	
   291	Null, list, and object/map param values reject. Empty-string **param values** are valid
   292	and preserved; empty target/profile and empty param keys reject. `params: {}` and
   293	omitted params both contribute no keys. Props reject `target`, `profile`, and `params`
   294	at their source paths. Boss has full parity with monster `place`.
   295	
   296	Top-level exact-ref defaults use the same shape:
   297	
   298	```yaml
   299	defaults:
   300	  'dnd5e:monsters:wolf':
   301	    target: wounded
   302	    profile: pack
   303	    params: { pursue: 6 }
   304	```
   305	
   306	Default keys are exact monster refs. Prop refs, families, aliases, prefixes, wildcards,
   307	and unknown refs reject.
   308	
   309	Target strings, profile strings, param keys, and their accepted values are opaque
   310	provider-defined vocabulary. v0.4 does not enumerate or interpret them. The compiler
   311	passes authored config to the applicable provider/spawn-config validation and reports
   312	any rejection at the exact source path. The API is a messenger and performs no
   313	behavior validation or calculation.
   314	
   315	### 6.2 Deterministic transport merge
   316	
   317	Config merges in three layers, lowest to highest:
   318	
   319	1. constructor/base config;
   320	2. exact-ref dungeon default;
   321	3. placement or boss config.
   322	
   323	For `target` and `profile`, a later present non-empty string replaces the earlier
   324	value. `params` merges key-wise; later present keys replace earlier keys. Omitted
   325	fields/keys leave the earlier layer unchanged. Explicit numeric zero, `false`, and
   326	empty-string param values are present values and MUST survive compile/persistence.
   327	An empty params map clears nothing because it contributes no keys.

   329	The merged opaque config is passed into compile/spawn data and encounter persistence.
   330	Profile and target remain authored opaque values; v0.4 does not require a resolved
   331	behavior preview or invent a separate typed authoring proto union.
   332	
   333	### 6.3 Preservation and projection
   334	
   335	Each monster/boss `FloorPlan.placements[]` entry echoes:
   336	
   337	- `source_path`, exact `ref`, and compiled absolute `at`;
   338	- optional authored `target` and `profile`; and
   339	- authored `params` with keys/JSON-scalar values preserved, including zero/false/
   340	  empty string.

   342	The compiled spawn config carries the three-layer merged `target`, `profile`, and
   343	key-wise params to the monster provider/DataJSON path. Provider validation errors use
   344	`ValidationError.field` with the placement/default source path and nested key suffix.

   346	
   347	Dungeon YAML MUST NOT contain mutable runtime state: current mode, machine state,
   348	knowledge/memory, stimuli, last-seen data, search/lapse counters, decision rationale,

   351	## 7. Tranche D — render-only environment lighting
   352	
   353	### 7.1 Source, inheritance, and mechanics boundary
   354	
   355	```yaml
   356	lighting: { ambient: 0.6 }
   357	regions:
   358	  - id: shrine
   359	    cells: [[3, 3], [3, 4]]
   360	    lighting: { ambient: 0.35 }
   361	```
   362	
   363	Document and region `lighting.ambient` are optional finite floats in `[0,1]`. An
   364	authored value is an absolute normalized renderer-intensity override, not a multiplier
   365	or theme-relative delta. Resolution walks innermost region → ancestors → document
   366	root and selects the nearest **authored** override.
   367	
   368	If no scope in that chain authors an override, effective ambient is absent. The game
   369	renderer/theme keeps its current baseline; the platform does not invent or publish a
   370	numeric default. This preserves existing surface differences (for example general
   371	versus crypt rendering) instead of falsely collapsing them to one constant. The compiler resolves authored override inheritance; the API passes the fields
   372	through without reinterpretation.
   373	
   374	Lighting is render-only. It MUST NOT change structural floor, wall/LoS tests,
   375	visibility, senses, reveal, fog authorization, target selection, or pathing. A darker
   376	override never hides an otherwise authorized hex and a brighter override never
   377	reveals one.
   378	
   379	Room-chain mode accepts document lighting only. Bounds-canvas unpainted cells use the
   380	root override when authored, otherwise no override. Region-floor cells use the nearest
   381	authored value in their innermost region chain, otherwise no override.
   382	
   383	### 7.2 Persistence and exact projection
   384	
   385	Authored YAML persists only raw lighting presence/value. Authored-content load
   386	recompiles optional effective overrides. A running encounter snapshot persists each
   387	hex's optional effective override (present or absent) so reload remains internally
   388	stable without consulting current authored YAML.
   389	
   390	Authoring projection is exact:
   391	
   392	- `FloorPlan.lighting` echoes the raw optional root block;
   393	- optional `FloorPlan.resolved_ambient` is present only when the root authors an
   394	  override;
   395	- each `FloorPlan.regions[]` entry echoes raw optional `lighting` and optional
   396	  `resolved_ambient`, present only when its inheritance chain finds an authored
   397	  override.
   398	
   399	Runtime `HexRecord.resolved_ambient` is optional. It is present on an authorized
   400	visible or remembered floor record only when that cell has an effective authored
   401	override; otherwise it is absent and the renderer/theme baseline remains in force.
   402	Hidden cells/regions and their lighting remain absent; there is no global runtime
   403	lighting/region map. The Tranche D probe discriminates support by requiring present
   404	`0.35` on the overridden parent/silent child and absence on the unrelated silent
   405	region, so an older server that omits every field does not falsely pass.
   406	
   407	## 8. Client-local compilation boundary
   408	
   409	`wallLines`, continuous wall footprints, fractional coverage, draft/raw masks, raw
   410	matrices/world coordinates, temporary IDs, UI selection/gizmos, snap previews, and
   411	uncommitted nudges are client-local. A builder may compile them losslessly into
   412	canonical region cells, `walls:`, or placement `offset` before validate-only.
   413	
   414	The platform accepts only canonical YAML and MUST NOT normatively cite or implement a
   415	specific TypeScript algorithm. Fractional coverage is never server standability. If
   416	a local construct cannot compile losslessly, the client hard-stops; it does not
   417	approximate or strip.
   418	
   419	## 9. Cross-layer acceptance specimens
   420	
   421	### 9.1 Irregular floor with interior void and pair envelope
   422	
   423	```yaml
   424	version: 1
   425	key: ring-room
   426	name: 'Ring Room'
   427	canvas: { width: 5, height: 5, floor_source: regions }
   428	rooms: []
   429	regions:
   430	  - id: ring
   431	    cells: [[1,1], [1,2], [1,3], [2,1], [2,3], [3,1], [3,2], [3,3]]
   432	```
   433	
   434	Validate-only returns exactly eight sorted cells, resolved `regions` source, present
   435	deterministic entrance at the first PartyCap-capable cell, and explicit solid pair
   436	edges around both outer void and `[2,2]`. Every envelope pair has exactly one floor
   437	owner, including off-canvas cases in an equivalent rim fixture. Non-validate writes,
   438	starts, encounter snapshot reload, pathing, target selection, placement, LoS, and fog agree
   439	on the same mask/edge truth.
   440	
   441	Removing a cell under dependent content rejects a write atomically, while
   442	validate-only still projects a structurally valid non-runnable candidate when the
   443	only failure is lifecycle seating/connectivity.
   444	
   445	### 9.2 Tiny draft and two islands
   446	
   447	A two-cell connected `floor_source: regions` mask is structurally valid:
   448	validate-only succeeds with cells/envelope and **absent** `FloorPlan.entrance`;
   449	non-validate rejects insufficient same-component PartyCap seating.
   450	
   451	A discriminating two-island mask contains a four-plus-cell PartyCap-capable island A
   452	and a one-cell island B. Validate-only succeeds, projects both islands and both
   453	envelopes, and may project entrance on A because its seats share A. Non-validate
   454	still rejects because B is outside the entrance component. Removing B makes the same
   455	candidate runnable. This proves entrance presence and whole-floor connectedness are
   456	separate gates.
   457	
   458	### 9.3 Placement offset survives a ref edit
   459	
   460	Initial submitted source:
   461	
   462	```yaml
   463	- ref: 'dnd5e:props:bookcase'
   464	  at: [3, 2]
   465	  facing: E
   466	  blocks_movement: true
   467	  blocks_los: true
   468	  offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.0]
   469	```
   470	
   471	Client-edited complete source:
   472	
   473	```yaml
   474	- ref: 'dnd5e:props:torch-ornate'
   475	  at: [3, 2]
   476	  facing: E
   477	  blocks_movement: false
   478	  blocks_los: false
   479	  offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.2]
   480	```
   481	
   482	There is no replacement call or persisted placement identity. Each document validates
   483	independently. Authoring/runtime return the submitted ref, absolute cell, facing,
   484	blockers, source path, and exact optional triple. The builder/game apply the same
   485	world-axis triple to the canonical origin. The torch's false/false authored blockers
   486	prove offset/model appearance does not become mechanics. A third candidate that
   487	retains `[0.05,0,0]` or omits offset is equally legal: ref changes have no implicit
   488	offset policy.
   489	
   490	### 9.4 Behavior transport defaults, placement override, and boss parity
   491	
   492	A provider-backed fixture accepts opaque values `target: wounded`, `profile: cautious`,
   493	and fixture params. Acceptance proves:
   494	
   495	- constructor/base → exact-ref default → placement/boss order;
   496	- target/profile later-present replacement and params key-wise replacement;
   497	- explicit numeric zero, false, and empty-string param values survive;
   498	- omitted params and `{}` contribute no keys and clear nothing;
   499	- room place, canvas place, and boss echo exact authored fields/source paths and pass
   500	  merged config to their spawn paths;
   501	- props reject, exact-ref defaults do not match another monster, and provider value
   502	  rejection is reported at the exact source path;
   503	- no runtime state appears in YAML.
   504	
   505	### 9.5 Lighting inheritance and fog authorization
   506	
   507	With root omitted, parent override `0.35` and silent child resolve the child to
   508	present `0.35`; an unrelated silent top-level region resolves to **absent**. With an
   509	authored root `0.6`, a silent unrelated region resolves to present `0.6`. Authoring
   510	projection distinguishes raw presence from optional effective presence. Authorized
   511	visible/remembered runtime hexes carry the override only where resolved; hidden
   512	region/hex data remains absent and authorized no-override hexes omit the field.
   513	Adversarial tests prove override changes cannot alter LoS, visibility, reveal, fog,
   514	or target selection.
