   412	canonical region cells, `walls:`, or placement `offset` before validate-only.
   413	
   414	The platform accepts only canonical YAML and MUST NOT normatively cite or implement a
   415	specific TypeScript algorithm. Fractional coverage is never server standability. If
   416	a local construct cannot compile losslessly, the client hard-stops; it does not
   417	approximate or strip.
   418	
   419	## 9. Cross-layer acceptance specimens
   420	
   421	### 9.1 Irregular floor with interior void and pair envelope
   422	
   423	```yaml
   424	version: 1
   425	key: ring-room
   426	name: 'Ring Room'
   427	canvas: { width: 5, height: 5, floor_source: regions }
   428	rooms: []
   429	regions:
   430	  - id: ring
   431	    cells: [[1,1], [1,2], [1,3], [2,1], [2,3], [3,1], [3,2], [3,3]]
   432	```
   433	
   434	Validate-only returns exactly eight sorted cells, resolved `regions` source, present
   435	deterministic entrance at the first PartyCap-capable cell, and explicit solid pair
   436	edges around both outer void and `[2,2]`. Every envelope pair has exactly one floor
   437	owner, including off-canvas cases in an equivalent rim fixture. Non-validate writes,
   438	starts, encounter snapshot reload, pathing, target selection, placement, LoS, and fog agree
   439	on the same mask/edge truth.
   440	
   441	Removing a cell under dependent content rejects a write atomically, while
   442	validate-only still projects a structurally valid non-runnable candidate when the
   443	only failure is lifecycle seating/connectivity.
   444	
   445	### 9.2 Tiny draft and two islands
   446	
   447	A two-cell connected `floor_source: regions` mask is structurally valid:
   448	validate-only succeeds with cells/envelope and **absent** `FloorPlan.entrance`;
   449	non-validate rejects insufficient same-component PartyCap seating.
   450	
   451	A discriminating two-island mask contains a four-plus-cell PartyCap-capable island A
   452	and a one-cell island B. Validate-only succeeds, projects both islands and both
   453	envelopes, and may project entrance on A because its seats share A. Non-validate
   454	still rejects because B is outside the entrance component. Removing B makes the same
   455	candidate runnable. This proves entrance presence and whole-floor connectedness are
   456	separate gates.
   457	
   458	### 9.3 Placement offset survives a ref edit
   459	
   460	Initial submitted source:
   461	
   462	```yaml
   463	- ref: 'dnd5e:props:bookcase'
   464	  at: [3, 2]
   465	  facing: E
   466	  blocks_movement: true
   467	  blocks_los: true
   468	  offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.0]
   469	```
   470	
   471	Client-edited complete source:
   472	
   473	```yaml
   474	- ref: 'dnd5e:props:torch-ornate'
   475	  at: [3, 2]
   476	  facing: E
   477	  blocks_movement: false
   478	  blocks_los: false
   479	  offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.2]
   480	```
   481	
   482	There is no replacement call or persisted placement identity. Each document validates
   483	independently. Authoring/runtime return the submitted ref, absolute cell, facing,
   484	blockers, source path, and exact optional triple. The builder/game apply the same
   485	world-axis triple to the canonical origin. The torch's false/false authored blockers
   486	prove offset/model appearance does not become mechanics. A third candidate that
   487	retains `[0.05,0,0]` or omits offset is equally legal: ref changes have no implicit
   488	offset policy.
   489	
   490	### 9.4 Behavior transport defaults, placement override, and boss parity
   491	
   492	A provider-backed fixture accepts opaque values `target: wounded`, `profile: cautious`,
   493	and fixture params. Acceptance proves:
   494	
   495	- constructor/base → exact-ref default → placement/boss order;
   496	- target/profile later-present replacement and params key-wise replacement;
   497	- explicit numeric zero, false, and empty-string param values survive;
   498	- omitted params and `{}` contribute no keys and clear nothing;
   499	- room place, canvas place, and boss echo exact authored fields/source paths and pass
   500	  merged config to their spawn paths;
   501	- props reject, exact-ref defaults do not match another monster, and provider value
   502	  rejection is reported at the exact source path;
   503	- no runtime state appears in YAML.
   504	
   505	### 9.5 Lighting inheritance and fog authorization
   506	
   507	With root omitted, parent override `0.35` and silent child resolve the child to
   508	present `0.35`; an unrelated silent top-level region resolves to **absent**. With an
   509	authored root `0.6`, a silent unrelated region resolves to present `0.6`. Authoring
   510	projection distinguishes raw presence from optional effective presence. Authorized
   511	visible/remembered runtime hexes carry the override only where resolved; hidden
   512	region/hex data remains absent and authorized no-override hexes omit the field.
   513	Adversarial tests prove override changes cannot alter LoS, visibility, reveal, fog,
   514	or target selection.
   515	
   516	## 10. Scope and ratification
   517	
   518	| In v0.4 | Client-local/not a wire construct | Above v0.4 |
   519	|---|---|---|
   520	| semantic region floor, explicit envelope pairs, draft/run lifecycle, deterministic entrance | `wallLines`, coverage masks, draft markers | authored holes primitive, levels, flat-top orientation |
   521	| optional verbatim placement `offset` | ref-replacement UI, raw transforms, uncommitted nudge state | prefabs/batch layout, arbitrary rotation/coloring |
   522	| opaque target/profile/params transport + exact-ref defaults | behavior calculations and runtime state | authored patrol/vision routes |
   523	| optional root/region ambient override inheritance/projection | renderer baseline/theme selection | per-source lights/environment gameplay |
   524	
   525	**Ratification record — 2026-08-08.** Kirk ruled that v0.4 is the pragmatic
   526	messenger/authoring shape recorded here, not a long-term ownership constitution. The
   527	bounded independent review of exact proposal head
   528	`0e97bc838f8d3bcc84852f58ee6b1383cb333ed2` returned **GO with zero
   529	field-shape/transport blockers**. v0.4 is therefore RATIFIED with no open spec-shape
   530	questions. PR #203 remains open as the tracking surface through downstream delivery.
   531	
   532	Relevant evidence: rpg-project PR #202 and
   533	[its platform handoff](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/202#issuecomment-5228001955),
   534	rpg-dnd5e-web [#728](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/728) /
   535	[PR #729](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/729), and delivered
   536	v0.3 Wave 0/1 evidence linked from the README.

1	# Dungeon YAML Spec v0.4 — context and rationale
     2	
     3	[`spec.md`](spec.md) is the normative **RATIFIED** delta over ratified v0.3. This
     4	README explains the pragmatic v0.x transport cut, its evidence, and how it relates to
     5	delivered v0.3. It does not add grammar.
     6	
     7	## What v0.4 is
     8	
     9	v0.4 is an authoring/transport shape for the next playable-scene increment, not a 2.0
    10	ownership constitution. It defines fields, preservation/projection, applicability,
    11	merge behavior where transport needs one, and cosmetic-versus-mechanical boundaries.
    12	It deliberately does not decide asset-pipeline governance, future behavior vocabulary,
    13	future provider internals or long-term platform ownership.
    14	
    15	The four additive tranches are:
    16	
    17	| Tranche | Pragmatic v0.4 shape |
    18	|---|---|
    19	| A — topology | canvas bounds versus explicit region-union floor, canonical mask/envelope, draft/run lifecycle |
    20	| B — placement | optional verbatim `offset: [x,y,z]` |
    21	| C — monster config | opaque optional `target`, `profile`, `params` plus exact-ref defaults |
    22	| D — lighting | optional inherited normalized ambient override, absent when unauthored |
    23	
    24	v0.3 Wave 0 and Wave 1 are both LIVE VERIFIED:
    25	[Wave 0](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/192#issuecomment-5206548237)
    26	and
    27	[Wave 1](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/180#issuecomment-5219362342).
    28	v0.4 is RATIFIED and still claims no implementation.
    29	
    30	## Authority and three axes
    31	
    32	v0.4 is honestly a normative **delta** over
    33	[`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md). Ratified v0.3 governs every omitted construct.
    34	
    35	Three axes stay separate:
    36	
    37	1. **v0.4** — documentation/review cut;
    38	2. **`version: 1`** — unchanged YAML decode version;
    39	3. **`canvas.floor_source: bounds | regions`** — canvas topology only, omission
    40	   resolving to legacy `bounds`.
    41	
    42	There is no YAML `spec:` or `draft` marker. Placement offset, monster config, and
    43	lighting do not depend on which floor-source mode is active.
    44	
    45	## Topology remains the strong core
    46	
    47	Kirk's direction remains:
    48	
    49	> “I think the floor is the region and we can see what is inside the walls. I think
    50	> the canvas is available space in the builder but only regions carry into the game.”
    51	
    52	`floor_source: regions` compiles the deduplicated union of `regions[].cells`. Canvas
    53	dimensions remain workspace/coordinate-legality bounds. Omission remains the v0.3
    54	rectangle so existing content never silently shrinks.
    55	
    56	### One mask and explicit envelope truth
    57	
    58	The compiled canonical mask feeds validation, placement, pathing, target reachability,
    59	start/PartyCap seating, walls, LoS, reveal/fog, encounter initialization, and
    60	projection. Subsystems do not independently recreate a rectangle or region union.
    61	
    62	Envelope wire reuses existing flat `FloorPlan.edges {from,to,kind}` pairs. Exactly one
    63	envelope endpoint is floor and owns the edge; the other is the adjacent void
    64	coordinate, including off-canvas coordinates. Pair order is nonsemantic. Runtime
    65	attaches the edge only to the owning floor `HexRecord`. This handles outer boundary
    66	and interior void without a new wire message or client derivation.
    67	
    68	### Draft validity versus runnable validity
    69	
    70	`validate_only` accepts structurally valid empty, too-small, and disconnected masks
    71	and always projects their floor/envelope. `FloorPlan.entrance` is absent until an
    72	anchor has a complete PartyCap seating envelope inside the same structural component;
    73	omitted-start candidates use deterministic canonical order.
    74	
    75	Non-validate requires nonempty floor, present entrance/seats, and every floor cell in
    76	the entrance component. The two-island specimen intentionally separates “can seat a
    77	party on island A” from “the authored floor is runnable as one component.”
    78	
    79	Union edits compile the complete candidate. Prior derived entrance/seats are discarded
    80	and freshly recomputed; they are not dependencies and may move. A strict write fails
    81	only when the candidate is not runnable or explicitly authored start/content/wall is
    82	invalidated. Nothing moves to root or widens back to bounds.
    83	
    84	### Two persistence lifecycles
    85	
    86	Authored load/write recompiles YAML and atomically replaces registered content.
    87	Encounter creation snapshots the exact mask/edges/config it starts with. Encounter
    88	reload checks snapshot consistency only and never compares current authored YAML.
    89	Future encounters see edits; running encounters retain their started world.
    90	
    91	### Region equality
    92	
    93	Same-region duplicate cells canonicalize. Between regions, equal or partial overlap
    94	rejects. That includes two empty regions: one empty region is legal, but two empties
    95	are equal sets and invalid.
    96	
    97	## Placement offset: the deliberately small composition transport
    98	
    99	The real-model work in web issue
   100	[#728](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/728), PR
   101	[#729](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/729), and its
   102	[evidence](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/blob/dev/docs/evidence/prop-composition-728.md)
   103	showed that a builder sometimes needs a small authored translation and that copying a
   104	complete old-asset transform is a poor replacement model. v0.4 takes only the useful
   105	transport lesson:
   106	
   107	```yaml
   108	offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.2]
   109	```
   110	
   111	The triple is three finite game-world `[x,y,z]` components relative to the canonical
   112	placement origin. It stays world-axis-aligned, is preserved/served verbatim, and the
   113	builder/game apply the same values. Existing ref/at/facing/mount applicability is
   114	unchanged.
   115	
   116	Offset is cosmetic. It cannot change owning cell, blockers, pathing, range,
   117	targetability, LoS, visibility, fog, or interaction identity. A client editing `ref`
   118	may retain, change, or remove offset in the complete submitted document; the server
   119	has no replacement command or implicit policy.
   120	
   121	That is the whole v0.4 composition contract. There is no anchor object, server
   122	replacement/stable placement ID, asset metadata, or raw matrix on the wire.
   123	
   124	## Monster config: opaque messenger fields
   125	
   126	Monster room/canvas placements and boss may carry:
   127	
   128	```yaml
   129	target: wounded
   130	profile: cautious
   131	params:
   132	  retreat_threshold: 0
   133	  announce: false
   134	```
   135	
   136	`target` and `profile` are nonempty opaque strings. `params` maps nonempty keys to
   137	JSON scalar bool/string/finite number. Null/list/object values reject. Zero, false,
   138	and empty-string param values remain present. Props reject all three fields.
   139	
   140	Exact-ref monster defaults use the same shape. Transport merge is deliberately small:
   141	constructor/base → exact-ref default → placement/boss. Later target/profile replaces
   142	when present; params merge key-wise with later keys winning. Omitted/empty params
   143	contribute no keys and clear nothing.
   144	
   145	The accepted target/profile strings, param keys, and value constraints are defined and
   146	validated by the applicable monster provider, not by v0.4. The compiler passes opaque
   147	values into compile/spawn config and reports rejection at source paths. The API merely
   148	carries fields. v0.4 does not enumerate strategies/profiles/knobs, define ranges,
   149	require a discovery protocol, special typed authoring union, or resolved behavior
   150	preview.
   151	
   152	Authoring projection echoes source path/ref/absolute cell plus authored target/profile/
   153	params. Spawn/encounter data receives the merged config. Mutable runtime mode, memory,
   154	perception, counters, chosen entity target, path, and other observations stay out of
   155	YAML.
   156	
   157	## Lighting: optional authored override
   158	
   159	Document/region `lighting.ambient` is an absolute normalized `[0,1]` renderer-intensity
   160	override. Inheritance selects the nearest authored value walking innermost → outward →
   161	root. If no scope authors one, effective override remains absent and the current
   162	renderer/theme baseline remains in force; different existing surfaces need not share
   163	a numeric default.
   164	
   165	Authoring projection echoes raw presence and optional inherited effective override.
   166	Authorized visible/remembered runtime hexes carry the optional effective override only
   167	where one exists. Hidden lighting remains absent.
   168	
   169	Lighting is render-only. It cannot affect floor, walls, LoS, senses, visibility,
   170	reveal, fog authorization, target selection, or pathing.
   171	
   172	## Normal capability behavior: validate, do not downgrade
   173	
   174	No named capability-key protocol is needed. The builder submits the exact candidate to
   175	`AuthoringService.PutDungeon(validate_only=true)`. Unsupported fields or values fail
   176	through normal source-path errors; success returns the specified projection.
   177	
   178	The client does not strip unsupported fields, substitute bounds floor, calculate
   179	opaque monster behavior, or erase offset/lighting to make a document pass. It either
   180	submits the exact authored semantics or hard-stops.
   181	
   182	## Client-local boundary
   183	
   184	`wallLines`, continuous footprints, fractional coverage, draft/raw masks, matrices/
   185	world transforms, temporary IDs, selection/gizmo state, snap previews, and uncommitted
   186	nudges remain client-local. A builder may compile them losslessly into canonical
   187	region cells, `walls:`, or committed `offset` before validation.
   188	
   189	The platform accepts canonical YAML and must not normatively cite a particular
   190	TypeScript implementation. Fractional coverage is never server standability. If local
   191	state cannot compile losslessly, the client stops instead of approximating it.
   192	
   193	## Reconciliation with delivered v0.3
   194	
   195	[`../../design.md`](../../design.md) and [`../../plan.md`](../../plan.md) remain the
   196	delivered v0.3 Wave 0/Wave 1 authority. Their rectangle floor, semantic-only region,
   197	unpainted root, and nonmutating-region statements remain correct under omitted/
   198	`floor_source: bounds`. Their “no lighting/geometry changes in #180” boundary remains
   199	true because #180 is complete.
   200	
   201	As ratified, explicit `floor_source: regions` narrowly changes those topology facts:
   202	region union becomes floor, union edits revalidate authored content, and unpainted
   203	cells are void. This scopes the conflict without rewriting completed delivery history.
   204	
   205	## Ratification record — 2026-08-08
   206	
   207	Kirk's ruling is the framing this final cut follows: v0.4 is a pragmatic v0.x
   208	messenger/authoring shape, not a long-term ownership constitution. After that
   209	simplification, bounded independent review of exact proposal head
   210	`0e97bc838f8d3bcc84852f58ee6b1383cb333ed2` returned **GO with zero
   211	field-shape/transport blockers**.
   212	
   213	v0.4 is therefore **RATIFIED**. No genuine spec-shape questions remain. Ratification
   214	approves the contract; it does not claim downstream implementation or close the
   215	tracking surface.
   216	
   217	## Acceptance pointers
   218	
   219	Normative specimens are in
   220	[`spec.md` §9](spec.md#9-cross-layer-acceptance-specimens):
   221	
   222	- irregular floor with interior void and one-sided pair envelope;
   223	- too-small draft and two islands;
   224	- placement offset preserved/changed across a client ref edit;
   225	- opaque behavior default/placement/boss merge with scalar presence; and
   226	- ambient override inheritance with present/absent and fog/mechanical assertions.
   227	
   228	Owning tracking issue: [#206](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/206).
   229	PR #203 remains the single review/tracking surface through downstream implementation.
   230	No implementation issues are created by this documentation revision.
   231	
   232	## Pointers
   233	
   234	- [`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md) and
   235	  [`../v0.3/README.md`](../v0.3/README.md) — ratified baseline.
   236	- [`../../design.md`](../../design.md) and [`../../plan.md`](../../plan.md) — delivered
   237	  v0.3 scope.
   238	- [PR #203](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/203) — ratified v0.4 tracking surface.
   239	- [PR #202 platform handoff](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/202#issuecomment-5228001955)
   240	  — behavior context; v0.4 intentionally keeps the values opaque.
   241	- [Web #728](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/728),
   242	  [PR #729](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/729), and
   243	  [evidence](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/blob/dev/docs/evidence/prop-composition-728.md)
   244	  — real-model evidence motivating a small offset transport, not a governance model.

   119	has no replacement command or implicit policy.
   120	
   121	That is the whole v0.4 composition contract. There is no anchor object, server
   122	replacement/stable placement ID, asset metadata, or raw matrix on the wire.
   123	
   124	## Monster config: opaque messenger fields
   125	
   126	Monster room/canvas placements and boss may carry:
   127	
   128	```yaml
   129	target: wounded
   130	profile: cautious
   131	params:
   132	  retreat_threshold: 0
   133	  announce: false
   134	```
   135	
   136	`target` and `profile` are nonempty opaque strings. `params` maps nonempty keys to
   137	JSON scalar bool/string/finite number. Null/list/object values reject. Zero, false,
   138	and empty-string param values remain present. Props reject all three fields.
   139	
   140	Exact-ref monster defaults use the same shape. Transport merge is deliberately small:
   141	constructor/base → exact-ref default → placement/boss. Later target/profile replaces
   142	when present; params merge key-wise with later keys winning. Omitted/empty params
   143	contribute no keys and clear nothing.
   144	
   145	The accepted target/profile strings, param keys, and value constraints are defined and
   146	validated by the applicable monster provider, not by v0.4. The compiler passes opaque
   147	values into compile/spawn config and reports rejection at source paths. The API merely
   148	carries fields. v0.4 does not enumerate strategies/profiles/knobs, define ranges,
   149	require a discovery protocol, special typed authoring union, or resolved behavior
   150	preview.
   151	
   152	Authoring projection echoes source path/ref/absolute cell plus authored target/profile/
   153	params. Spawn/encounter data receives the merged config. Mutable runtime mode, memory,
   154	perception, counters, chosen entity target, path, and other observations stay out of
   155	YAML.
   156	
   157	## Lighting: optional authored override
   158	
   159	Document/region `lighting.ambient` is an absolute normalized `[0,1]` renderer-intensity
   160	override. Inheritance selects the nearest authored value walking innermost → outward →
   161	root. If no scope authors one, effective override remains absent and the current
   162	renderer/theme baseline remains in force; different existing surfaces need not share
   163	a numeric default.
   164	
   165	Authoring projection echoes raw presence and optional inherited effective override.
   166	Authorized visible/remembered runtime hexes carry the optional effective override only
   167	where one exists. Hidden lighting remains absent.
   168	
   169	Lighting is render-only. It cannot affect floor, walls, LoS, senses, visibility,
   170	reveal, fog authorization, target selection, or pathing.
   171	
   172	## Normal capability behavior: validate, do not downgrade
   173	
   174	No named capability-key protocol is needed. The builder submits the exact candidate to
   175	`AuthoringService.PutDungeon(validate_only=true)`. Unsupported fields or values fail
   176	through normal source-path errors; success returns the specified projection.
   177	
   178	The client does not strip unsupported fields, substitute bounds floor, calculate
   179	opaque monster behavior, or erase offset/lighting to make a document pass. It either
   180	submits the exact authored semantics or hard-stops.
   181	
   182	## Client-local boundary
   183	
   184	`wallLines`, continuous footprints, fractional coverage, draft/raw masks, matrices/
   185	world transforms, temporary IDs, selection/gizmo state, snap previews, and uncommitted
   186	nudges remain client-local. A builder may compile them losslessly into canonical
   187	region cells, `walls:`, or committed `offset` before validation.
   188	
   189	The platform accepts canonical YAML and must not normatively cite a particular
   190	TypeScript implementation. Fractional coverage is never server standability. If local
   191	state cannot compile losslessly, the client stops instead of approximating it.
   192	
   193	## Reconciliation with delivered v0.3
   194	
   195	[`../../design.md`](../../design.md) and [`../../plan.md`](../../plan.md) remain the
   196	delivered v0.3 Wave 0/Wave 1 authority. Their rectangle floor, semantic-only region,
   197	unpainted root, and nonmutating-region statements remain correct under omitted/
   198	`floor_source: bounds`. Their “no lighting/geometry changes in #180” boundary remains
   199	true because #180 is complete.
   200	
   201	As ratified, explicit `floor_source: regions` narrowly changes those topology facts:
   202	region union becomes floor, union edits revalidate authored content, and unpainted
   203	cells are void. This scopes the conflict without rewriting completed delivery history.
   204	
   205	## Ratification record — 2026-08-08
   206	
   207	Kirk's ruling is the framing this final cut follows: v0.4 is a pragmatic v0.x
   208	messenger/authoring shape, not a long-term ownership constitution. After that
   209	simplification, bounded independent review of exact proposal head
   210	`0e97bc838f8d3bcc84852f58ee6b1383cb333ed2` returned **GO with zero
   211	field-shape/transport blockers**.
   212	
   213	v0.4 is therefore **RATIFIED**. No genuine spec-shape questions remain. Ratification
   214	approves the contract; it does not claim downstream implementation or close the
   215	tracking surface.
   216	
   217	## Acceptance pointers
   218	
   219	Normative specimens are in
   220	[`spec.md` §9](spec.md#9-cross-layer-acceptance-specimens):
   221	
   222	- irregular floor with interior void and one-sided pair envelope;
   223	- too-small draft and two islands;
   224	- placement offset preserved/changed across a client ref edit;
   225	- opaque behavior default/placement/boss merge with scalar presence; and
   226	- ambient override inheritance with present/absent and fog/mechanical assertions.
   227	
   228	Owning tracking issue: [#206](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/206).
   229	PR #203 remains the single review/tracking surface through downstream implementation.
   230	No implementation issues are created by this documentation revision.
   231	
   232	## Pointers
   233	
   234	- [`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md) and
   235	  [`../v0.3/README.md`](../v0.3/README.md) — ratified baseline.
   236	- [`../../design.md`](../../design.md) and [`../../plan.md`](../../plan.md) — delivered
   237	  v0.3 scope.
   238	- [PR #203](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/203) — ratified v0.4 tracking surface.
   239	- [PR #202 platform handoff](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/202#issuecomment-5228001955)
   240	  — behavior context; v0.4 intentionally keeps the values opaque.
   241	- [Web #728](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/728),
   242	  [PR #729](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/729), and
   243	  [evidence](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/blob/dev/docs/evidence/prop-composition-728.md)
   244	  — real-model evidence motivating a small offset transport, not a governance model.

--- 2b188a4
commit 2b188a400977b6128770ee5592f4e4f28e076075
parents 3ee1efbc214d5e77ddcbe84dea6acc1cdae86f1a
author Kirk Gilmore <kirklgilmore@gmail.com>
date 2026-08-08T11:25:01-07:00
subject spec(dungeon-builder): Dungeon YAML v0.4 (PROPOSED) — the floor is the region
body Transcribes Kirk's 2026-08-08 ruling ("the floor is the region... the canvas
is available space in the builder but only regions carry into the game")
into a normative delta on ratified v0.3: canvas-mode structural floor
becomes the union of declared region cells, with implicit envelope walls at
every floor/void boundary — dissolving v0.3's rim-edge inexpressibility
(a 1x1 canvas's 6 boundary edges, all unauthorable under v0.3, all implicit
here). Also promotes wallLines's client-projection contract, region-scoped
lighting, decor-grade height/offset, and introduces the spec: document field
as the floor-semantics discriminator so v0.3 canvas documents keep their
existing meaning with no migration.

Not yet ratified — see README.md's "Open ratification points" for what
still needs Kirk/platform sign-off before the header flips to RATIFIED.

— asset-pipeline agent, on behalf of KirkDiggler

--- 9b2fd75
commit 9b2fd754198c780ce21c7e976972125d705ca28a
parents 2b188a400977b6128770ee5592f4e4f28e076075
author Kirk Gilmore <kirklgilmore@gmail.com>
date 2026-08-08T14:12:41-07:00
subject spec(dungeon-builder): broaden proposed v0.4 authored scene
body Replace the overloaded spec marker with a semantic canvas floor source and
cut topology, prop composition, monster behavior, and environment into
independently implementable tranches. Reconcile the delivered v0.3 docs,
real-model composition evidence, and Phase-1 behavior handoff while keeping
the contract proposed.

— rpg-project member, on behalf of KirkDiggler

--- 7814808
commit 781480803293119a8d5caf36b92215978bb83643
parents 9b2fd754198c780ce21c7e976972125d705ca28a
author Kirk Gilmore <kirklgilmore@gmail.com>
date 2026-08-08T14:35:54-07:00
subject spec(dungeon-builder): close v0.4 lifecycle and wire gaps
body Make each authored-scene tranche independently probeable only with its full
projection path, separate authored and encounter persistence, and define strict
draft/run topology lifecycle. Reuse canonical edge pairs for envelopes, narrow
prop composition to authored intent, split behavior merge chains, and make
lighting render-only with an exact fog-safe projection.

— rpg-project member, on behalf of KirkDiggler

--- c37a1e1
commit c37a1e118148cf3890cdaedba9a215674169cc5b
parents 781480803293119a8d5caf36b92215978bb83643
author Kirk Gilmore <kirklgilmore@gmail.com>
date 2026-08-08T14:48:05-07:00
subject spec(dungeon-builder): correct lighting and behavior wire
body Preserve renderer/theme lighting baselines when no authored override exists,
close behavior projection with a typed scalar union, and make freshly derived
PartyCap seating authoritative for each authored candidate.

— rpg-project member, on behalf of KirkDiggler

body Keep region-union topology as the strong contract while reducing composition,
monster config, lighting, and capability handling to pragmatic v0.x authored
fields and normal validate-only transport behavior.

— rpg-project member, on behalf of KirkDiggler

   377	   follow-up findings where an existing surface can report them; this wave adds no
   378	   diagnostics proto/API and makes none an acceptance requirement.
   379	8. Region create/edit/delete operations MUST NOT alter structural floor, canonical
   380	   wall/door edges, door identity, or the validity of any content (placement/
   381	   monster/boss) whose cell falls inside the edited region. Content whose owning
   382	   region is deleted MUST fall back to the next enclosing scope. Connector `DoorID`
   383	   (room-ID-derived, `compile.go:301`) and authored-edge `AuthoredDoorID`
   384	   (endpoint-derived, `authored_edges.go:32-36`) are both region-independent and
   385	   MUST NOT be recomputed by a region edit.
   386	
   387	#### 4.10.3 Structural validation and persistence
   388	
   389	1. Hard rejection is limited to source that cannot be represented safely or
   390	   deterministically: malformed YAML/types/coordinates; duplicate region IDs; a
   391	   cell outside structural floor; incompatible non-empty `rooms:` with `regions:`;
   392	   an unsupported explicit archetype; and equal or partial overlap between regions,
   393	   which prevents a unique innermost owner.
   394	2. Within one region, duplicate cell pairs are canonically deduplicated before
   395	   compile and persistence; no error or new diagnostic surface is required. A
   396	   region's canonical source cells may be empty or disconnected in this exploratory
   397	   phase.
   398	3. Disjoint sets and strict containment resolve per §4.10.2.2. Regions need not
   399	   tile the canvas; sparse, disconnected regions with unclaimed cells are valid.
   400	4. An inner wall (§4.7) MUST NOT alter a region's canonical source-cell membership.
   401	5. Persistence retains only irreducible authored region facts: `id`, `name`,
   402	   archetype presence/value, and canonical source cells. Parent relationships and
   403	   the innermost cell index are deterministic derived state: recompute them on
   404	   compile/load. They MUST NOT be persisted, and a missing or disagreeing derived
   405	   cache MUST NOT reject reload.
   406	6. A document combining non-empty `rooms:` with declared `regions:` MUST be
   407	   rejected — a document declares exactly one topology model, never both.
   408	
   409	#### 4.10.4 Wire projection
   410	
   411	**Authoring** — `FloorPlan` MUST project, for each declared region: its `cells:`
   412	extent and a toolkit-derived parent region id (absent means root). This is in
   413	addition to, not a replacement for, the per-hex runtime projection below. This
   414	projection exposes derived scope structure; it creates no semantic validation.
   415	
   416	**Runtime**:
   417	
   418	| Field | Type | Semantics |
   419	|---|---|---|
   420	| `HexRecord.zone_id` | string | innermost region id for this cell; `""` = root |
   421	| `Zone.parent_id` | string, optional | derived parent region id; absent = root |
   422	
   423	1. Runtime projection MUST expose `Zone.parent_id` and per-hex innermost `zone_id`,
   424	   fog-authorized: expose the innermost zone and required ancestor chain only for
   425	   cells the observing player has seen. A global hidden cell-to-region map MUST NOT
   426	   be exposed. This projection creates no semantic validation.
   427	
   428	#### 4.10.5 Extension seam
   429	
   430	1. This cut adds no properties to `RegionDoc` beyond `id`/`name`/`archetype`/
   431	   `cells`. A future spec level adding one MUST resolve it through the same
   432	   per-property innermost-outward walk (§4.10.2.5).
   433	
   434	**Acceptance criteria:**
   435	- A structurally usable graph compiles and reloads with zero, one, or multiple
   436	  explicitly declared `entrance`, `boss`, `chamber`, and `corridor` regions, and
   437	  with disconnected or empty regions. Missing roles are non-blocking and need no
   438	  new diagnostic wire surface.
   439	- Duplicate IDs, out-of-floor cells, unsupported explicit archetypes, equal/partial
   440	  overlaps, and incompatible non-empty `rooms:` plus `regions:` reject clearly.
   441	  Duplicate cells within one region canonicalize to one source cell.
   442	- Parent-ID/innermost-index derivation is deterministic across compile/load and
   443	  repaint/delete, without persisting derived state or rejecting a missing/disagreeing
   444	  derived cache.
   445	- `archetype: boss` labels a semantic scope only; no boss entity/cell, monster
   446	  marker, content placement rule, or spawn behavior is required. Ordinary top-level
   447	  `place:` monsters remain ordinary placements.
   448	- Authoring `FloorPlan` projects each declared region's canonical `cells:` extent
   449	  and toolkit-derived parent id; runtime projects `Zone.parent_id` and per-hex
   450	  innermost `zone_id`, fog-authorized, with no hidden-extent disclosure. These
   451	  projections create no semantic validation.
   452	- No region boundary appears as a `FloorPlanEdge` record unless an independent
   453	  `walls:` entry (§4.7) also exists on that same edge.

1	# Dungeon Walls: straight modular walls at the room envelope
     2	
     3	**Status:** design for review
     4	**Parent:** rpg-project#132 (Dungeon visual fidelity umbrella) · relates to `ideas/dungeon-authoring/` (PR #121) · supersedes the render layer of rpg-toolkit#848 (whose findings report is this design's data reference)
     5	
     6	## Problem
     7	
     8	Walls are rendered per hex cell today: the client draws each wall entry the
     9	toolkit emits, cell by cell. On a hex grid that produces zig-zag "teeth" along
    10	every room edge, plus the degenerate rubble blocks flanking doors diagnosed in
    11	toolkit#848. It also fights the art direction: the Synty POLYGON Dungeon pack —
    12	and the promo shot that is this initiative's quality bar — is built from
    13	straight modular wall segments, corner pieces, and doorway frames. As long as
    14	walls follow hex boundaries, those assets cannot be used as designed.
    15	
    16	## Principle
    17	
    18	> toolkit is the rules, we are the presentation — Kirk, 2026-07-25
    19	
    20	The hex grid is the *rules* model: walkability, movement, LOS, blocking —
    21	server-authoritative (the server already rejects invalid movement; client
    22	clickability follows the same data). The wall *mesh* is presentation, and
    23	nothing requires presentation to be hex-shaped. This design splits the layers:
    24	
    25	- **Toolkit (rules): unchanged.** Cells, doors, blocking, LOS stay exactly as
    26	  emitted today. Zero toolkit/proto/api changes in v1.
    27	- **Client (presentation):** stops rendering room-boundary wall entries.
    28	  Instead it derives **wall runs** — straight segments along each room's outer
    29	  envelope *and along each connector column* — and lays Synty modular pieces
    30	  (segments, corners, door frames) along them.
    31	
    32	**Corollary (the invisible-wall rule): every server-side blocker must have a
    33	visual representation.** Blocking is server-authoritative and unaffected by
    34	what the client draws — but a blocked cell rendered as open floor is a worse
    35	bug than ugly walls. The runs below cover every boundary and connector blocker.
    36	
    37	## Geometry
    38	
    39	- **Room envelope runs**: the wall line sits at the **outer envelope** of each
    40	  room's playable hex region — the straight bounding line at the outermost
    41	  cell extent per side.
    42	- **Connector runs**: adjacent rooms are separated by a reserved one-column
    43	  gap that belongs to no room (that gap *is* the connector — see
    44	  Implementation notes). The gap's non-door cells are real server-side
    45	  blockers, so the client draws **one straight wall along each connector
    46	  column**, with the opening at the door cell. This replaces today's rubble
    47	  blocks with the same visual language as the rest of the walls.
    48	- The one hard constraint (Kirk): **character models standing in any playable
    49	  cell must not clip through the wall.** Boundary-cell centers sit at least
    50	  half a hex from the envelope, so an envelope-line wall with standard Synty
    51	  thickness clears standard character radius — verify with the largest
    52	  character/monster mesh before locking the offset. If clipping appears, push
    53	  the wall outward; never mask cells to solve clipping.
    54	- **No cells are masked.** Every cell playable today stays playable and
    55	  clickable; there are no exposed hex teeth — the wall thickness swallows the
    56	  scallops.
    57	- The half-hex scallop strip between the offset columns' floor tiles and the
    58	  wall base is covered by presentation: extend the floor slab / skirting to
    59	  the wall line.
    60	
    61	## What the client's data actually says (toolkit#848 findings)
    62	
    63	The wire already separates everything this design needs (full detail in the
    64	findings report on toolkit#848):
    65	
    66	- **Props vs walls are different channels.** Obstacles (pillars, coffins,
    67	  braziers, …) ride the *entities* list as Obstacle payloads with content refs
    68	  and per-viewer reveal gating. Walls are a flat, unconditional per-room list.
    69	  No ambiguity to resolve.
    70	- **Within the walls list**: boundary-edge entries (`From != To`) are room
    71	  boundaries — under this design the client stops rendering these and draws
    72	  envelope/connector runs instead. Degenerate entries (`From == To`) are
    73	  interior pattern walls — those **still render** (the crypt has them; the
    74	  reference tomb doesn't). Door entries carry `Kind = DOOR_*` and the only
    75	  non-nil `Id`s in the list — they key door-frame placement and locked-state
    76	  rendering exactly as today (lock DC/ability stay server-side).
    77	- Rules are untouched by any of this: movement/LOS blocking is rebuilt
    78	  server-side from the data and never reads the client's mesh choices.
    79	- **Region membership is per-viewer reveal-gated** (added post-review): the
    80	  hex membership reaching a client is the REVEALED subset (sight-range gated),
    81	  not full room membership — while the walls list is whole-room and
    82	  unconditional. Any geometry derived from region hexes therefore tracks the
    83	  player's explored frontier, not the room. Caught by gate review on the W1
    84	  implementation; governed by the section below.
    85	
    86	## Fog of war / partial reveal (v1 decision, 2026-07-25)
    87	
    88	Because region membership is reveal-gated, runs derived from it follow the
    89	explored frontier. v1 decisions:
    90	
    91	- **Envelope runs trace the frontier.** The wall line sits at the edge of the
    92	  explored area and steps outward as more of the room is revealed — accepted
    93	  as the fog-of-war visual for v1; revisit after Kirk's walk if it reads
    94	  badly. (Future alternative needing no backend change: derive full-room
    95	  envelopes from the unconditional walls channel, which already carries
    96	  whole-room boundary edges.)
    97	- **Two-tier exception, now load-bearing (PR #626):** a region's row extent
    98	  tracks its own frontier exactly as above UNLESS it participates in a
    99	  validated connector, in which case it may snap early to the connector's
   100	  proven extent via the shared-Height assumption (every region shares one
   101	  `DungeonParams.Height`, so widening to a peer's proven extent is never
   102	  wrong geometry — just early). Isolated regions, and regions whose peer
   103	  hasn't revealed further either, still track the frontier. Column extent is
   104	  never widened this way — room widths genuinely differ, unlike height.
   105	- **Connector coverage must not depend on reveal state.** Doors pair to the
   106	  nearest region on each side (not exact column adjacency), and — the
   107	  structural guarantee — any connector-flanking wall entry not covered by an
   108	  emitted run FALLS BACK to per-cell rendering. The invisible-wall rule is
   109	  enforced by construction, not by hoping reveal state cooperates.
   110	- The clip-clearance dial's default is ~√3 hex units, not 1.0 — the row
   111	  staircase eats 0.69–0.87 of a nominal offset (measured in review); W4 tunes
   112	  from there.
   113	- Different-height adjacent rooms: connector runs take the union of the two
   114	  row ranges — fine at uniform height (all current content), documented as a
   115	  known v1 limit.
   116	- **Load-bearing coupling (for any future server change):** the client
   117	  derives true grid bounds from `Wall.from` min/max over the walls list,
   118	  which works because walls are projected whole-room and never reveal-gated
   119	  (the proto exposes no space dimensions). If per-viewer wall reveal is ever
   120	  added server-side, that derivation silently narrows and the invisible-wall
   121	  class returns — put this on that change's checklist.
   122	- **Wall height and cutaway now exist** (PR #626): a `?wallHeight=` dial and
   123	  a `?wallCutaway=1` prototype classifying each run/partition as
   124	  camera-facing (stub) or away-facing (tall), including a peel-away rule for
   125	  connector doors/walls that sit between the camera and the player's own
   126	  current room — see that PR for the full geometry and Kirk's default-look
   127	  decision.
   128	
   129	## Implementation notes (feeds plan.md)
   130	
   131	From the toolkit#848 findings — the traps a web implementer must respect:
   132	
   133	- No per-room width/offset exists on the wire: derive each room's bounding
   134	  rect as min/max over `RegionData.Hexes`. `Space.Width/Height` is the
   135	  combined space, not the room.
   136	- The reserved one-column gap between consecutive rooms belongs to no region's
   137	  `Hexes` — that's the connector column, not a data error. A cell in bounds,
   138	  in no region, and not a door position is a connector flanking cell.
   139	- Every door in a dungeon sits on the same `doorRow = height/2`. Boss rooms
   140	  have their entire doorRow deliberately open across their full width
   141	  (toolkit#819 tactical invariant) — not a generation bug.
   142	- Hex adjacency must use real cube/neighbor math (the six direction vectors /
   143	  `HexNeighbors`), never same-row column-stepping: in the odd-q scheme,
   144	  stepping to an adjacent column changes row depending on column parity.
   145	  Same-column row steps are safe.
   146	
   147	## Deferred (explicitly out of v1)
   148	
   149	- **Breakable wall sections.** If wanted later, an authored `place:`-able
   150	  breakable-wall prop with its own mesh — not a property of every wall cell.
   151	  (Wave 1 persists no destructibility model; emitted walls are indestructible.)
   152	- **Toolkit-emitted wall runs.** If the server ever needs runs (destructible
   153	  runs, procedural wall variation), promote run computation into the toolkit
   154	  and project it. v1 keeps it client-derived because it is pure presentation
   155	  policy with zero proto/api/toolkit churn.
   156	- **Interior pattern-wall restyle.** Crypt-style interior walls keep their
   157	  current per-cell rendering in v1; restyling them to modular pieces can
   158	  follow once the envelope/connector language is proven.
   159	
   160	## Interim: toolkit PR #849
   161	
   162	PR #849 (the original #848 fix, already implemented and live-verified) merges
   163	independently of this design as the interim improvement: it converts the
   164	connector rubble to uniform boundary-edge walls in the *current* renderer, so
   165	doors look right now, and leaves the walls list uniformly shaped for this
   166	design's filter. This design later supersedes how those entries are drawn —
   167	not their existence or their blocking role.
   168	
   169	## Verification
   170	
   171	Screenshot-judged (per the team's rigor calibration: visual work is judged by
   172	the harness + Kirk's eyes against the Synty bar, not review machinery):
   173	
   174	- reference-tomb before/after at matching camera angles;
   175	- clip-check with the largest model standing in boundary cells on both the
   176	  flush and scalloped columns;
   177	- door areas at both connectors — frame, opening, locked-state rendering;
   178	- Kirk walks it.
   179	
   180	## Rollout
   181	
   182	1. toolkit#848 findings are on the issue (done — data reference for this doc).
   183	2. toolkit PR #849 merges as the interim fix (independent track).
   184	3. Web implementation issue in rpg-dnd5e-web (asset-pipeline team, client
   185	   seams): envelope + connector run computation, modular wall placement, floor
   186	   skirt, boundary-entry render filter. Replaces the old boundary-wall
   187	   rendering outright.
   188	4. Kirk walk + screenshot set; asset gaps found along the way feed the M3
   189	   backlog.
   190	
   191	— asset-pipeline agent, on behalf of KirkDiggler

     9	
    10	## Issue / PR structure
    11	
    12	- **One implementation issue** in rpg-dnd5e-web (sub-issue of rpg-project#132;
    13	  board 19: Feature="The Dungeon", Team=Assets, Kind=Build) with the four
    14	  slices below as its checklist.
    15	- **Two PRs**: PR-A = W1+W2 (run computation + placeholder render — the first
    16	  visible win), PR-B = W3+W4 (Synty meshes + tuning). Each PR lands runnable
    17	  with screenshot evidence — no long dark stretches.
    18	- Repo law: `npm run ci-check` before push; playtest-evidence screenshots on
    19	  the PR; ready-for-review only, never draft.
    20	
    21	## W1 — Run computation (pure module + tests)
    22	
    23	A pure module (`wallRuns` or similar): inputs are exactly what the encounter
    24	map already receives — regions' hex sets, doors, and grid bounds derived from
    25	the unconditional walls list (`Wall.from` min/max — the proto exposes no
    26	space-dimension fields; as-built correction, see design.md's load-bearing
    27	coupling note); outputs are per-room **envelope runs** and per-connector
    28	**column runs** in world coordinates, each with door gaps.
    29	
    30	Rules (from the design's implementation notes):
    31	- Room bounding rect = min/max over the region's `Hexes` (no width/offset
    32	  fields exist on the wire).
    33	- Connector column = in-bounds cells belonging to no region; the door cell
    34	  (from Doors data) splits that column's run into two segments.
    35	- Use the client's existing hex→world transform for endpoints; never assume
    36	  same-row column adjacency (odd-q parity — real neighbor math only).
    37	- Envelope line = outer envelope + a configurable outward offset (the
    38	  clip-clearance dial, tuned in W4).
    39	
    40	**Acceptance:** unit tests against a reference-tomb-shaped fixture (3 rooms,
    41	2 connectors, shared doorRow, locked door) plus a boss-room fixture (the
    42	deliberately open full-width doorRow must NOT produce gaps in the envelope).
    43	
    44	## W2 — Render runs + category filter (placeholder geometry)
    45	
    46	Replace boundary-wall rendering in the encounter map with a **positive
    47	category rule** — draw exactly these, and nothing else in the walls channel:
    48	
    49	- (a) W1's runs, as straight placeholder geometry (simple extruded boxes);
    50	- (b) interior pattern walls — degenerate (`From == To`) entries whose cell
    51	  lies inside a region's hex set (crypt has these; reference-tomb doesn't);
    52	- (c) door frames keyed off door entries (`Kind = DOOR_*`, the only non-nil
    53	  `Id`s), oriented along the connector column axis — not off
    54	  `doorPassageNeighbor`'s arbitrary first-neighbor pick.
    55	
    56	Because the rule is positive, it renders correctly against both the
    57	pre-#849 wire (degenerate connector flanks) and the post-bump wire
    58	(boundary-edge flanks) without branching. Also in this slice: extend the
    59	floor slab/skirting to the wall line (cover the half-hex scallops).
    60	
    61	**Acceptance:** reference-tomb screenshot set — both door areas and all four
    62	sides of each room; explicit invisible-wall check (every connector flanking
    63	cell visually covered by its run); ci-check green. **This is the first
    64	visible milestone: screenshots go to Kirk before W3 starts.**
    65	
    66	## W3 — Synty modular pieces
    67	
    68	- Inventory the POLYGON Dungeon wall modules already in the contract tree
    69	  (`harness/models/synty/`) vs. those needing ingest from the source pack
    70	  (`scripts/ingest-assets.sh` → rpg-game-assets flow). Asset gaps here are
    71	  our own pipeline work, not blockers on someone else.
    72	- Map runs to segment / corner / door-frame pieces; theme-appropriate
    73	  material/tint via `Space.theme`; locked-door visual preserved.
    74	
    75	**Acceptance:** side-by-side screenshots against the Synty promo bar,
    76	matching camera angles on the door areas.
    77	
    78	## W4 — Clip-check, tuning, Kirk walk
    79	
    80	- Clip-check with the largest character/monster mesh standing in boundary
    81	  cells on both flush and scalloped columns — no clipping; tune W1's offset
    82	  dial outward if needed, never mask cells.
    83	- Kirk walks the reference tomb. Findings triage: render bugs fix in PR-B;
    84	  asset-quality gaps (mesh/material/glow) go to the M3 backlog.
    85	
    86	## Review rigor (calibrated)
    87	
    88	W1 carries the only real logic — unit tests plus one review pass. W2–W4 are
    89	presentation: judged by the screenshot harness and Kirk's eyes against the
    90	bar, light single-pass review, no confirm ceremony.
    91	
    92	## Traps for the implementer (do not rediscover)
    93	
    94	- Screenshot harness on game routes needs `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` —
    95	  the encounter stream holds networkidle open forever.
    96	- Kill vite by port (`lsof -ti :3001`), never `pkill -f vite` (self-match).
    97	- GLBs cache hard: hard-reload after any asset sync. `npm run assets:sync`
    98	  pulls rpg-game-assets' default branch only and is `rsync --delete`.
    99	- If wire fields look missing locally: stale installed protos —
   100	  `rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install`.
   101	- Always start a fresh encounter after an api image swap (Redis persists).
   102	
   103	**Pointers:** design = `design.md` in this folder · wire-data facts = the
   104	findings comment on toolkit#848 · hex parity math =
   105	`tools/spatial/position.go:176-217` (toolkit).
   106	
   107	— asset-pipeline agent, on behalf of KirkDiggler

The W1 gate review found the design had missed that region membership
(RegionData.Hexes) reaching the client is per-viewer reveal-gated
(sight-range/explored-subset), not full room membership -- while the
walls list itself is whole-room and unconditional. Any geometry derived
from region hexes therefore tracks the player's explored frontier, not
the room.

  visual, revisit after Kirk's walk if it reads badly; a full-room
  alternative exists later via the unconditional walls channel with no
  backend change).

  flanking wall entry not covered by an emitted run falls back to
  per-cell rendering -- the invisible-wall rule enforced by
  construction, not by hoping reveal state cooperates.
- Clip-clearance dial default corrected to ~sqrt(3) hex units (not 1.0)
  -- the row staircase eats 0.69-0.87 of a nominal offset, measured in
  review.
- Different-height adjacent rooms take the union of the two row ranges
  for v1 (documented limit, not a defect at today's uniform-height
  content).

load-bearing: a region's row extent tracks its own frontier unless it

substance.

(?wallHeight=, ?wallCutaway=1), including the peel-away partition rule for
connector doors/walls between the camera and the player's own room —

decision.

* docs(ideas): dungeon-walls design absorbs toolkit#848 findings — connector runs, wire-data facts, implementation notes

Revises the design now that toolkit#848's investigation has landed:

- Connector columns get their own wall runs (not just room-envelope runs) --
  the reserved one-column gap between rooms is a real server-side blocker,
  so it needs the same visual language as room boundaries, not the old
  rubble blocks. New "invisible-wall rule" corollary: every server-side
  blocker must have a visual representation.
- "What the client's data actually says" replaces open questions with the
  findings' facts: props/walls are separate wire channels, boundary-edge
  vs degenerate-interior wall entries are already distinguishable, door
  entries carry Kind/Id.
- New "Implementation notes" section: room bounding rects derive from
  RegionData.Hexes (no per-room width/offset on the wire), the reserved
  connector column isn't a data error, doorRow = height/2 with boss rooms
  open across the full row, and hex adjacency needs real cube/neighbor
  math (not same-row column-stepping).
- New "Interim: toolkit PR #849" section: the interim rubble-to-boundary-
  edge fix merges independently, ahead of this design's own client-side
  rendering change.
- Verification gains a door-areas screenshot check (frame/opening/locked
  state at both connectors).

* docs(ideas): dungeon-walls design absorbs W1 gate finding — reveal-gated regions, fog v1 decision (#133)

The W1 gate review found the design had missed that region membership
(RegionData.Hexes) reaching the client is per-viewer reveal-gated
(sight-range/explored-subset), not full room membership -- while the
walls list itself is whole-room and unconditional. Any geometry derived
from region hexes therefore tracks the player's explored frontier, not
the room.

New "Fog of war / partial reveal (v1 decision, 2026-07-25)" section:

- Envelope runs trace the explored frontier for v1 (accepted fog-of-war
  visual, revisit after Kirk's walk if it reads badly; a full-room
  alternative exists later via the unconditional walls channel with no
  backend change).
- Connector coverage must not depend on reveal state: any connector-
  flanking wall entry not covered by an emitted run falls back to
  per-cell rendering -- the invisible-wall rule enforced by
  construction, not by hoping reveal state cooperates.
- Clip-clearance dial default corrected to ~sqrt(3) hex units (not 1.0)
  -- the row staircase eats 0.69-0.87 of a nominal offset, measured in
  review.
- Different-height adjacent rooms take the union of the two row ranges
  for v1 (documented limit, not a defect at today's uniform-height
  content).

* docs(ideas): dungeon-walls as-built — wireGridBounds coupling note + W1 input correction (#133)

design.md: adds a load-bearing coupling note under the fog-of-war section —
the client derives true grid bounds from Wall.from min/max over the walls
list (works today because walls are whole-room and never reveal-gated); if
per-viewer wall reveal is ever added server-side, that derivation silently
narrows and the invisible-wall class returns. Flagged for any future
server-side wall-reveal change's checklist.

plan.md: corrects W1's inputs to match — grid bounds come from Wall.from
min/max, not "combined space dimensions" (the proto exposes no
space-dimension fields).

diff --git a/ideas/dungeon-builder/spec/v0.4/README.md b/ideas/dungeon-builder/spec/v0.4/README.md
index a0c576c..3fd4ae7 100644
--- a/ideas/dungeon-builder/spec/v0.4/README.md
+++ b/ideas/dungeon-builder/spec/v0.4/README.md
@@ -1,108 +1,108 @@
 # Dungeon YAML Spec v0.4 — context and rationale
 
-[`spec.md`](spec.md) is the normative **PROPOSED** delta over ratified v0.3. This
+[`spec.md`](spec.md) is the normative **RATIFIED** delta over ratified v0.3. This
 README explains the pragmatic v0.x transport cut, its evidence, and how it relates to
 delivered v0.3. It does not add grammar.
 
 ## What v0.4 is
 
 v0.4 is an authoring/transport shape for the next playable-scene increment, not a 2.0
 ownership constitution. It defines fields, preservation/projection, applicability,
 merge behavior where transport needs one, and cosmetic-versus-mechanical boundaries.
 It deliberately does not decide asset-pipeline governance, future behavior vocabulary,
 future provider internals or long-term platform ownership.
 
 The four additive tranches are:
 
 | Tranche | Pragmatic v0.4 shape |
 |---|---|
 | A — topology | canvas bounds versus explicit region-union floor, canonical mask/envelope, draft/run lifecycle |
 | B — placement | optional verbatim `offset: [x,y,z]` |
 | C — monster config | opaque optional `target`, `profile`, `params` plus exact-ref defaults |
 | D — lighting | optional inherited normalized ambient override, absent when unauthored |
 
 v0.3 Wave 0 and Wave 1 are both LIVE VERIFIED:
 [Wave 0](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/192#issuecomment-5206548237)
 and
 [Wave 1](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/180#issuecomment-5219362342).
-v0.4 remains PROPOSED and claims no implementation.
+v0.4 is RATIFIED and still claims no implementation.
 
 ## Authority and three axes
 
 v0.4 is honestly a normative **delta** over
 [`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md). Ratified v0.3 governs every omitted construct.
 
 Three axes stay separate:
 
 1. **v0.4** — documentation/review cut;
 2. **`version: 1`** — unchanged YAML decode version;
 3. **`canvas.floor_source: bounds | regions`** — canvas topology only, omission
    resolving to legacy `bounds`.
 
 There is no YAML `spec:` or `draft` marker. Placement offset, monster config, and
 lighting do not depend on which floor-source mode is active.
 
 ## Topology remains the strong core
 
 Kirk's direction remains:
 
 > “I think the floor is the region and we can see what is inside the walls. I think
 > the canvas is available space in the builder but only regions carry into the game.”
 
 `floor_source: regions` compiles the deduplicated union of `regions[].cells`. Canvas
 dimensions remain workspace/coordinate-legality bounds. Omission remains the v0.3
 rectangle so existing content never silently shrinks.
 
 ### One mask and explicit envelope truth
 
 The compiled canonical mask feeds validation, placement, pathing, target reachability,
 start/PartyCap seating, walls, LoS, reveal/fog, encounter initialization, and
 projection. Subsystems do not independently recreate a rectangle or region union.
 
 Envelope wire reuses existing flat `FloorPlan.edges {from,to,kind}` pairs. Exactly one
 envelope endpoint is floor and owns the edge; the other is the adjacent void
 coordinate, including off-canvas coordinates. Pair order is nonsemantic. Runtime
 attaches the edge only to the owning floor `HexRecord`. This handles outer boundary
 and interior void without a new wire message or client derivation.
 
 ### Draft validity versus runnable validity
 
 `validate_only` accepts structurally valid empty, too-small, and disconnected masks
 and always projects their floor/envelope. `FloorPlan.entrance` is absent until an
 anchor has a complete PartyCap seating envelope inside the same structural component;
 omitted-start candidates use deterministic canonical order.
 
 Non-validate requires nonempty floor, present entrance/seats, and every floor cell in
 the entrance component. The two-island specimen intentionally separates “can seat a
 party on island A” from “the authored floor is runnable as one component.”
 
 Union edits compile the complete candidate. Prior derived entrance/seats are discarded
 and freshly recomputed; they are not dependencies and may move. A strict write fails
 only when the candidate is not runnable or explicitly authored start/content/wall is
 invalidated. Nothing moves to root or widens back to bounds.
 
 ### Two persistence lifecycles
 
 Authored load/write recompiles YAML and atomically replaces registered content.
 Encounter creation snapshots the exact mask/edges/config it starts with. Encounter
 reload checks snapshot consistency only and never compares current authored YAML.
 Future encounters see edits; running encounters retain their started world.
 
 ### Region equality
 
 Same-region duplicate cells canonicalize. Between regions, equal or partial overlap
 rejects. That includes two empty regions: one empty region is legal, but two empties
 are equal sets and invalid.
 
 ## Placement offset: the deliberately small composition transport
 
 The real-model work in web issue
 [#728](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/728), PR
 [#729](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/729), and its
 [evidence](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/blob/dev/docs/evidence/prop-composition-728.md)
 showed that a builder sometimes needs a small authored translation and that copying a
 complete old-asset transform is a poor replacement model. v0.4 takes only the useful
 transport lesson:
 
 ```yaml
 offset: [0.05, 0.0, 0.2]
@@ -121,123 +121,124 @@ has no replacement command or implicit policy.
 That is the whole v0.4 composition contract. There is no anchor object, server
 replacement/stable placement ID, asset metadata, or raw matrix on the wire.
 
 ## Monster config: opaque messenger fields
 
 Monster room/canvas placements and boss may carry:
 
 ```yaml
 target: wounded
 profile: cautious
 params:
   retreat_threshold: 0
   announce: false
 ```
 
 `target` and `profile` are nonempty opaque strings. `params` maps nonempty keys to
 JSON scalar bool/string/finite number. Null/list/object values reject. Zero, false,
 and empty-string param values remain present. Props reject all three fields.
 
 Exact-ref monster defaults use the same shape. Transport merge is deliberately small:
 constructor/base → exact-ref default → placement/boss. Later target/profile replaces
 when present; params merge key-wise with later keys winning. Omitted/empty params
 contribute no keys and clear nothing.
 
 The accepted target/profile strings, param keys, and value constraints are defined and
 validated by the applicable monster provider, not by v0.4. The compiler passes opaque
 values into compile/spawn config and reports rejection at source paths. The API merely
 carries fields. v0.4 does not enumerate strategies/profiles/knobs, define ranges,
 require a discovery protocol, special typed authoring union, or resolved behavior
 preview.
 
 Authoring projection echoes source path/ref/absolute cell plus authored target/profile/
 params. Spawn/encounter data receives the merged config. Mutable runtime mode, memory,
 perception, counters, chosen entity target, path, and other observations stay out of
 YAML.
 
 ## Lighting: optional authored override
 
 Document/region `lighting.ambient` is an absolute normalized `[0,1]` renderer-intensity
 override. Inheritance selects the nearest authored value walking innermost → outward →
 root. If no scope authors one, effective override remains absent and the current
 renderer/theme baseline remains in force; different existing surfaces need not share
 a numeric default.
 
 Authoring projection echoes raw presence and optional inherited effective override.
 Authorized visible/remembered runtime hexes carry the optional effective override only
 where one exists. Hidden lighting remains absent.
 
 Lighting is render-only. It cannot affect floor, walls, LoS, senses, visibility,
 reveal, fog authorization, target selection, or pathing.
 
 ## Normal capability behavior: validate, do not downgrade
 
 No named capability-key protocol is needed. The builder submits the exact candidate to
 `AuthoringService.PutDungeon(validate_only=true)`. Unsupported fields or values fail
 through normal source-path errors; success returns the specified projection.
 
 The client does not strip unsupported fields, substitute bounds floor, calculate
 opaque monster behavior, or erase offset/lighting to make a document pass. It either
 submits the exact authored semantics or hard-stops.
 
 ## Client-local boundary
 
 `wallLines`, continuous footprints, fractional coverage, draft/raw masks, matrices/
 world transforms, temporary IDs, selection/gizmo state, snap previews, and uncommitted
 nudges remain client-local. A builder may compile them losslessly into canonical
 region cells, `walls:`, or committed `offset` before validation.
 
 The platform accepts canonical YAML and must not normatively cite a particular
 TypeScript implementation. Fractional coverage is never server standability. If local
 state cannot compile losslessly, the client stops instead of approximating it.
 
 ## Reconciliation with delivered v0.3
 
 [`../../design.md`](../../design.md) and [`../../plan.md`](../../plan.md) remain the
 delivered v0.3 Wave 0/Wave 1 authority. Their rectangle floor, semantic-only region,
 unpainted root, and nonmutating-region statements remain correct under omitted/
 `floor_source: bounds`. Their “no lighting/geometry changes in #180” boundary remains
 true because #180 is complete.
 
-If ratified, explicit `floor_source: regions` narrowly changes those topology facts:
+As ratified, explicit `floor_source: regions` narrowly changes those topology facts:
 region union becomes floor, union edits revalidate authored content, and unpainted
 cells are void. This scopes the conflict without rewriting completed delivery history.
 
-## Review state
+## Ratification record — 2026-08-08
 
-The prior non-shape “ratification gates” were governance rather than ambiguities in
-the v0.4 field/transport shape, and are removed. This document remains **PROPOSED** until a bounded consistency review confirms
-the simplified messenger shapes and topology rules.
+Kirk's ruling is the framing this final cut follows: v0.4 is a pragmatic v0.x
+messenger/authoring shape, not a long-term ownership constitution. After that
+simplification, bounded independent review of exact proposal head
+`0e97bc838f8d3bcc84852f58ee6b1383cb333ed2` returned **GO with zero
+field-shape/transport blockers**.
 
-**Genuine remaining spec-shape questions:** none currently identified. Review may
-still find one; resolve any concrete ambiguity in PR #203 before changing the status.
-Do not flip to RATIFIED merely because the artificial gates are gone.
+v0.4 is therefore **RATIFIED**. No genuine spec-shape questions remain. Ratification
+approves the contract; it does not claim downstream implementation or close the
+tracking surface.
 
 ## Acceptance pointers
 
 Normative specimens are in
 [`spec.md` §9](spec.md#9-cross-layer-acceptance-specimens):
 
 - irregular floor with interior void and one-sided pair envelope;
 - too-small draft and two islands;
 - placement offset preserved/changed across a client ref edit;
 - opaque behavior default/placement/boss merge with scalar presence; and
 - ambient override inheritance with present/absent and fog/mechanical assertions.
 
 Owning tracking issue: [#206](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/206).
 PR #203 remains the single review/tracking surface through downstream implementation.
 No implementation issues are created by this documentation revision.
 
 ## Pointers
 
 - [`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md) and
   [`../v0.3/README.md`](../v0.3/README.md) — ratified baseline.
 - [`../../design.md`](../../design.md) and [`../../plan.md`](../../plan.md) — delivered
   v0.3 scope.
-- [PR #203](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/203) — proposed v0.4 review
-  and tracking surface.
+- [PR #203](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/203) — ratified v0.4 tracking surface.
 - [PR #202 platform handoff](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/202#issuecomment-5228001955)
   — behavior context; v0.4 intentionally keeps the values opaque.
 - [Web #728](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/728),
   [PR #729](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/729), and
   [evidence](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/blob/dev/docs/evidence/prop-composition-728.md)
   — real-model evidence motivating a small offset transport, not a governance model.

@@ -1,83 +1,83 @@
 # Dungeon YAML Spec v0.4
 
-**Status:** PROPOSED v0.4, 2026-08-08. Not yet ratified.
+**Status:** RATIFIED v0.4, 2026-08-08.
 **Normative delta.** RATIFIED v0.3
 ([`../v0.3/spec.md`](../v0.3/spec.md)) remains the complete baseline. This file
 changes only the constructs and rules it names. Unmentioned v0.3 grammar and behavior
 remain normative. Context copied here is for reading continuity, not a claim that this
 file restates every v0.3 field.
 
 See [`README.md`](README.md) for evidence, reconciliation, and ratification history.
 
 ## 1. Three distinct axes
 
 | Axis | Value | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | Documentation cut | v0.4 | This proposal/review surface; never a YAML field. |
 | Dungeon document version | `version: 1` | Unchanged persisted YAML decode version. |
 | Canvas floor source | `canvas.floor_source: bounds \| regions` | Canvas topology only; omission resolves to `bounds`. |
 
 There is no `spec:` field. `spec: "0.4"`, `spec: draft`, and other documentation or
 workflow markers MUST fail strict decode. Behavior and environment fields are
 additive and independent of canvas floor-source choice.
 
 ## 2. Additive transport shapes and capability behavior
 
 v0.4 adds four separable shapes. Each section defines decode/validation,
 preservation, authoring projection, runtime transport, and mechanical boundary.

 projection. Subsystems do not independently recreate a rectangle or region union.

 Authored load/write recompiles YAML and atomically replaces registered content.

@@ -121,123 +121,124 @@ has no replacement command or implicit policy.
